3.title: System counters and SMC readings
3.content: | Property | System counters | SMC readings | . | What they are | Processor time, memory, swap, startup volume space, and network and storage byte counters that macOS keeps | Temperatures, fan speeds, voltages, currents and power from the System Management Controller (SMC) | . | How they are read | Public macOS calls: host_processor_info, host_statistics64, sysctl, statfs, getifaddrs and the IOKit storage driver statistics | The AppleSMC IOKit service, with read-only commands, for a fixed table of keys | . | Picker groups | CPU, Memory, Storage, Network | CPU, GPU, Battery, Fans, System | . | On the measured M5 Pro | 14 readings: 9 read directly, 5 worked out from two reads | 38 readings | . | On another Mac | The same collectors run; a counter macOS does not return is left out | Depends on the model and chip (see SMC readings) | . | Minimum, maximum, average | Not provided; Mac Sensors keeps its own from its reads | Not provided; Mac Sensors keeps its own from its reads | . | Access needed | No administrator access | No administrator access, privileged helper or driver | . Neither source keeps a history, so Mac Sensors keeps statistics for every reading itself. A key with Value shown on Minimum, Maximum or Average, or a press that cycles to them, shows the lowest, highest or average value accepted for that reading since the plugin last started reading sensors. They start over after a gap in that reading; see How are MIN, MAX and AVG calculated on a key? Dial statistics are separate local observations; see Sensor Dial. The plugin only reads. The native reader has no command that writes an SMC key or changes a fan, and it exposes no hardware handle to the rest of the plugin.

4.title: System counters
4.content: | Reading | Group | Unit | How the plugin gets it | . | CPU usage | CPU | % | Share of processor ticks that were not idle between two reads, across every core | . | Memory total | Memory | bytes | Installed memory (hw.memsize) | . | Memory free, Memory active, Memory inactive, Memory wired, Memory compressed | Memory | bytes | The kernel’s page counts for each category, times the page size | . | Swap used | Memory | bytes | Swap in use (vm.swapusage) | . | Startup volume total, Startup volume available | Storage | bytes | Size and space available on the volume mounted at / | . | Network receive, Network send | Network | bytes per second | Change in received and sent bytes between two reads, summed over Ethernet-type interfaces named en0, en1 and so on | . | Storage read, Storage write | Storage | bytes per second | Change in bytes read and written between two reads, summed over every block storage driver | . The memory readings are the kernel’s named counters. Their sum is not Activity Monitor’s Memory Used, and the plugin does not compute one. Network and storage rates are totals for the Mac. They are not split by application, interface or drive. Only interfaces named en followed by a number count, so loopback, VPN tunnel and bridge interfaces are left out. The five worked-out readings (CPU usage and the four rates) need two reads, so they are left out of a read when there is no valid pair: . | the first read after reading starts (see Counter rebaseline); | the first system counter read after one that failed or arrived too old, which starts a new pair; | a counter that went down, which means it was reset or started over; | a change in which interfaces or storage drivers are counted; | a sleep between the two reads, detected when the time elapsed and the time awake differ by more than 50 ms; | for the storage rates, any block storage driver that reports no byte counts, on every read where it does so; | for the network rates, no interface named en followed by a number. | . When a worked-out reading is left out, a key showing only that reading shows Sensor missing until the next read brings it back. Its sparkline starts again. Known limit in 1.0.1: network counters start over at 4 GiB. macOS gives the plugin 32-bit byte counters for each interface. When one passes 4 GiB it starts again from zero, and the read in which that happens shows no network rate. At a sustained 1 Gbit/s that is about every 34 seconds for each direction and interface. At Read every 5 seconds, a transfer of more than 4 GiB within one read would also be undercounted.

5.title: SMC readings
5.content: The native reader opens the AppleSMC service and, for each key in its table, asks for the key’s type and size once per connection, then reads its value on every read. Its transport accepts three read-only SMC commands and rejects any other command before it reaches the SMC. It checks the reply’s length and firmware status, decodes the types flt, sp78, fpe2, ui8, ui16 and ui32, and withholds anything else. The table has 61 candidate SMC keys. Keys that the SMC on this Mac does not have are left out. | Applies to | SMC keys | Readings | . | Every Mac | 31 | CPU and GPU diode and proximity, battery and Airport temperatures; memory and DC In voltage; CPU and GPU high side, DC In and battery current; CPU package, GPU, battery, DC In, memory and system power; Fan 1 to Fan 8 | . | Mac computers with Apple silicon | 4 more | Airflow left, Airflow right, NAND and Battery 2 temperatures | . | Mac17,9 with the t6050 chip only | 26 more | CPU super core and performance core temperatures, GPU 1 to GPU 8 temperatures | . On the measured Mac17,9 with an M5 Pro, 38 of the 61 SMC keys answer. Any other model with Apple silicon receives the first two rows, and an Intel Mac the first row only; on both, the plugin log records This model uses common typed sensors; its generation-specific catalog is not qualified. A Mac without fans need not report fan readings. For the state of Intel validation, see Hardware compatibility. Each kind of reading has a range. A value outside it is withheld, never shown: . | Kind | Unit | Accepted range | . | Temperature | °C | -50 to 150 | . | Fan | RPM | 0 to 30,000 | . | Voltage | V | 0 to 100 | . | Current | A | -500 to 500 | . | Power | W | -1,000 to 2,000 | . A successful zero stays zero; an idle power rail or a stopped fan can read 0. If the AppleSMC service is missing or cannot be opened, the SMC readings are left out and the system counters keep working. The support report records the error under sourceErrors. A transport failure closes the SMC connection, and the next read opens it again. These are not offered in 1.0.1: CPU and GPU clocks, GPU usage, per-chip power channels, and HID temperature sensors. The HID registrations had duplicate identities and invalid values, and the power and clock channels found were metadata without a qualified meaning. A value that can be decoded is not offered unless its meaning is known.

6.title: Reading identity
6.content: A saved reading is stored by its identity, never by its label or position in the list. | A system counter’s identity is its name, for example mac:v1:system:cpu-total. It is the same on every Mac, so a saved CPU usage selection works on another Mac. | An SMC reading’s identity is the Mac model, the four key bytes and a meaning revision, for example mac:v1:smc:Mac17%2C9:54423154:temp.v1 for the battery temperature on a Mac17,9. A selection saved on one model shows Sensor missing on another model. The plugin does not move it to a reading with a similar name. | . Labels, list order and the plugin build are not part of the identity, so renaming a label in a later version cannot point a saved key at a different sensor. Two rows that produce the same identity are both withheld. A row whose key bytes are not four printable characters, or whose model name cannot be encoded, is withheld. The settings panel’s picker shows the readings of the latest read, grouped as CPU, GPU, Memory, Storage, Network, Battery, Fans and System. The list updates on its own when a source adds or removes readings; that update does not start an extra read.

7.title: How a read works
7.content: One reader serves every Sensor Reading key (including the Back tile), Sensor Dial and detail tile on every connected deck. It starts when the first of them appears and stops 2 seconds after the last one disappears, unless one appears again within those 2 seconds. The plugin log says, for example, Started (1000 ms interval) and Stopped (no visible actions). Sensor Control keys do not keep it running. See When reading starts and stops. Each read asks both sources. Each source runs its hardware calls on its own background slot, so a slow SMC read never blocks the system counters. If a source’s previous read has not returned yet, it is not asked again until it has. Every reading carries its own acquisition time, taken when its read started, not when the answer arrived. A late answer therefore cannot make an older value look newer.

8.title: One redraw per read
8.content: When a key or dial shows readings from both sources, the source that answers first waits for the other, so the face changes once for that read instead of twice: . | The wait lasts at most 100 ms. If the other source has not answered by then, the first source’s readings appear and the other’s follow when they arrive. | After eight reads in a row in which both sources answered within 50 ms of each other, the plugin stops applying the 100 ms limit. | On the next slow read it waits once for the second source, for up to one Read every interval, then applies the 100 ms limit again until there are eight fast reads in a row. | The 100 ms limit always applies while keys and dials show a status screen, for example Reading sensors or No sensor data, so a slow source never holds a recovery back. | The count of fast reads starts over when reading starts and when Read every changes. A page change inside the 2 seconds keeps it. A Read every change also shows any readings still waiting at once. | . Waiting changes only when the face is drawn. It never changes a reading’s acquisition time, and each read still adds one sparkline point and one dial observation. In a traced run of an earlier 1.0.1 candidate, measured as a development copy in the Stream Deck app on the M5 Pro at 1 second, the two sources of a read answered a median 11.5 ms apart and at most 40.2 ms apart (PERF.md). In a separate terminal benchmark of the native reader, two windows of 1,000 reads at 1 second, the SMC part of a read had a median of 11.52 ms and 11.10 ms; the slowest read, 66.39 ms, was in the first window (PERF.md, scripts/bench-native.mjs). How long SMC reads take on an Intel Mac is unknown; a source that answers more than 100 ms after the other can change the face twice in one read.

9.title: Counter rebaseline
9.content: The first system counter read after reading starts only sets the starting point for CPU usage and the rates. About a quarter second later the plugin reads the system counters once more, so those readings appear without waiting a full Read every interval: . | The extra read starts 250 ms after the first read started, and never sooner than 200 ms after the first read finished. The kernel counts processor time in 10 ms ticks, so 200 ms covers about twenty. | It happens once each time reading starts: when a key, dial or detail tile appears and none was visible for the last 2 seconds, for example the first one after the plugin starts, or a page you return to after that long. A page change, opening sensor details or pressing Back inside the 2 seconds keeps the baseline, so CPU usage and the rates carry on without this read. | If the regular read is due first, as at Read every 250 ms, the regular read takes its place. | A regular read that starts within 200 ms after the extra read started reads only the SMC, so CPU usage and the rates are never computed over a gap of only a few milliseconds. | . Until the extra read, a key that shows only CPU usage or a rate shows Sensor missing. In an earlier 1.0.1 release candidate, measured as a development copy in the Stream Deck app on the M5 Pro, CPU usage showed a value a median 253.6 ms after a key appeared, over 40 appearances (PERF.md, 2026-10-16 actual-app entry). That candidate had no 2 second hold, so each of those appearances started reading. Check again in a settings panel reads at once, so CPU usage and rates from that read cover the time since the read before it, which can be a fraction of a second.

10.title: Read every
10.content: Read every sets how often the plugin reads both sources. It is under Advanced, Connection, marked All keys and dials, in both the Sensor Reading and Sensor Dial panels. It is one setting for the whole plugin, not one per key. Connection also says that the plugin reads available sensors on this Mac and does not change hardware settings, that available readings depend on this Mac and macOS version, and that a saved reading stays selected when it is unavailable. It holds Sensor setup, three first steps (see Status screens). | Option | Notes | . | 250 ms | Shortest. Uses the most processor time | . | 500 ms |   | . | 1 second | Default | . | 2 seconds |   | . | 5 seconds | Longest. Inside the 15-second reading lifetime | . The Connection summary shows the effective value, for example “Mac sensors · read every 1 s”. | One read serves every key, dial and detail tile, so this is the plugin’s total read rate. Adding keys does not add reads. | Changing it clears the sparkline history of every key and dial. It keeps every reading’s MIN, MAX and AVG and every dial’s session statistics. The plugin log records each change, for example Read interval set to 500 ms. | A blank or non-numeric stored value means 1 second. A stored number outside the range is read as the nearest end, so a value above 5 seconds, for example from a configuration document, runs at 5 seconds, and one below 250 ms runs at 250 ms. A number inside the range that the menu does not offer, such as 1500, is used as stored. The stored setting itself is never rewritten. | Each read asks both sources for new measurements. How often the SMC itself refreshes a key is unknown, so an SMC value can repeat between reads. | . Shorter intervals use more processor time. As a development copy in the Stream Deck app on the M5 Pro with 32 single-reading keys, the published 1.0.1.0 used 0.704% of one core at 1 second over 24 hours, and an earlier 1.0.1 candidate used 0.668% at 1 second and 2.478% at 250 ms (PERF.md). An earlier 1.0.1 release candidate in the repository mock host (scripts/lib/mock-host.mjs) with six actions used 18 to 19 ms of plugin CPU time per second at 250 ms, about 5 ms at 1 second and about 1 ms at 5 seconds; the app’s own drawing cost is not included (PERF.md).

11.title: When reading starts and stops
11.content: The plugin reads sensors while at least one Sensor Reading key (the Back tile of a detail page included), Sensor Dial or detail tile is visible on any deck. Sensor Control keys do not count. | Reading starts when one of them appears while reading is stopped: the first time after the plugin starts, or after none has been visible for 2 seconds. Keys show Reading sensors until the first read returns, CPU usage and the transfer rates follow about a quarter second later (Counter rebaseline), and the plugin log says Started (… ms interval). | When the last one disappears, the plugin makes no new regular reads but keeps the reading for 2 seconds. The Stream Deck app removes the old page’s actions before it shows the new page’s, so changing pages, opening sensor details and pressing Back leave a moment with nothing visible. If one appears again within the 2 seconds, the same reading continues. Key MIN, MAX and AVG, sparklines, the counter baseline, the count of fast reads and dial sessions are kept. Keys show readings at once instead of Reading sensors, CPU usage and the rates do not wait for a new pair, and the log shows no new Started line. The next read comes on the next Read every tick. | Reading stops 2 seconds after the last one disappeared, if none has appeared since. The plugin closes its reader, clears every sparkline, ends every reading’s MIN, MAX and AVG, and logs Stopped (no visible actions). The next appearance starts reading as above, and a dial that returns then shows stats reset: data gap once. | . The 2 seconds is fixed. This comes from the code and its software tests; how long a page change takes on a physical deck has not been measured.

12.title: Freshness and local history
12.content: Each reading expires 15 seconds after its own acquisition time and is then removed, at that moment rather than at the next read. Ages are measured on a clock that keeps counting while the Mac sleeps, so changing the system clock cannot extend a reading’s life. With Read every at most 5 seconds, a source that keeps answering replaces its readings long before they expire. | A read that fails removes that source’s readings at once. The other source keeps serving. One exception: SMC readings wait for the first successful system counter read, which carries the font check. Until then keys show Source error, or Source busy if a read is still out after 15 seconds. | A row that is invalid, out of range, not a finite number or duplicated is withheld. | The plugin never draws an expired or failed reading as live. It has no held-value state: a reading is current or it is absent, and an absent reading shows Sensor missing on its key or Sensor missing / waiting on its dial (see Status screens). | An unchanged value can be a genuine new measurement. A hardware register that stopped changing internally cannot be told apart from a steady one by reading it. | Nothing is shown before the first successful read: keys and dials show Reading sensors until then. | . Sparklines add one point for each new acquisition, not for each redraw, and keep up to 36 points spaced by reads, not by time. A sparkline starts again when its reading is absent or not a finite number, when the reading’s unit or type changes, when keys show a status screen, when Read every changes, and when reading stops, 2 seconds after the last Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile disappears. Returning to a page after none was visible anywhere for 2 seconds therefore starts its sparklines over. A page change, opening sensor details or pressing Back inside the 2 seconds keeps every sparkline, and while one stays visible, a hidden key’s sparkline keeps filling. Each reading’s MIN, MAX and AVG take one sample from each accepted read of it. A reading that is withheld, removed by a failed read or expired, or whose unit or type changes, starts its statistics over at its next accepted read, and every reading starts over when reading stops, 2 seconds after the last Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile disappears. A Read every change keeps them, and so does a page change inside those 2 seconds. See Value shown. Dial minimum, maximum and average are local session statistics from new observations; a redraw of the same observation does not count again. See Sensor Dial.

13.title: Sleep and wake
13.content: This section describes the code and its software tests. Real sleep and wake on a Mac with a deck attached has not been checked yet; that check is pending. | After a sleep longer than 15 seconds, every reading is past its limit, and the plugin removes them at its first read or expiry check after the wake. Every reading’s MIN, MAX and AVG start over with its first read after the wake. Until then the deck can still show the face drawn before the sleep; how long that lasts on a physical deck is unknown. Until the first read after waking returns, keys and dials can then show No sensor data. A read that starts from a status screen always uses the 100 ms limit, so system readings return at most 100 ms after their read completes, even when the SMC read is slow. In software tests with a simulated 60-second sleep and a slow first SMC read, the status screen lasted at most 105 ms: a 5 ms system read plus the 100 ms limit. Whether that screen is visible on a physical deck is unknown. | After any sleep, the first system counter read detects the sleep and leaves out CPU usage and the rates for that read, so they return one Read every interval later, with their MIN, MAX and AVG started over. No extra rebaseline read is made. | After a sleep shorter than 15 seconds, readings taken before the sleep stay current until their own 15 seconds run out or the next read replaces them. A reading other than CPU usage and the rates that is read again before its 15 seconds run out keeps its MIN, MAX and AVG. | . If a screen stays after waking, see Keys show No sensor data.

15.title: Data sources
15.content: Every reading on a key, dial or detail tile comes from one of two local sources on this Mac: macOS system counters, or SMC readings taken by the plugin’s own native reader. Each read asks both sources. There is no source setting to choose and no separate sensor application. Which readings exist depends on the Mac model and macOS version. For requirements and the Tahoma Bold prerequisite, see Installation and requirements. For what was measured on which Mac, see Hardware compatibility.

17.content: With Custom selected, one select per gesture appears. Touch zones stays below them, as on Elite. 18.title: Rotation groups
18.content: Optional, and nothing changes until you build them. Split the rotation set into named groups: a plain turn stays inside the active group, and a pressed turn on Elite (or any turn set to Switch sensor or group on Custom) jumps to the next group. The dial shows the landing group’s name on its stats line for a moment. Build them in the dial’s settings panel, under Reading: . | Split into groups under the rotation list turns your current set into group 1 and adds an empty group 2, where new ticks then land. | The radio in front of a group (New ticks land in this group) marks where ticks land. Tick readings in the search above the lists and they join that group; the search’s label then names it, for example Readings for group 2. A freshly opened panel marks the group that holds the reading on the dial. | Earlier and Later at a group’s edge move the selected reading into the neighboring group. Option with Left or Right Arrow does the same from the list, Option+Home or Option+End moves it to either end of its group, and Delete takes it out of the set. | Each group has an optional name, such as CPU, GPU or Cooling. An unnamed group shows on the dial as group 2 and so on. | Add group appends another group and marks it for new ticks. The × on a group removes it, and its readings leave the rotation. Merge back into one set flattens everything into a plain rotation set again. | A line under the lists says what this dial’s gestures do with the groups. When no gesture can switch groups (Legacy, or Custom without Switch sensor or group), it says turns run through all groups as one list, in group order, with a Change gestures link. | . Removing a group that holds readings, and a merge that would drop a group name or fold two or more groups of readings into one, ask for a second press. The first press arms the button, which then says what goes, for example Remove GPU and its 2 readings? or Merge and drop the group names?. A quick double click only arms it. An empty group goes at once. How groups behave: . | Groups take effect once two of them hold readings; until then rotation runs as one flat list. A reading belongs to the first group that holds it. | The active group is wherever the reading on the dial lives. A group jump moves it, and so do a Sensor Control key and an alert interrupt. On a preset that can switch groups, turn after any of those and you step inside the group you landed in. A group whose readings are all missing is skipped by the jump. | On those presets, the auto cycle steps inside the active group and the overviews list it. With Auto cycle jumps to a critical reading ticked, the cycle still watches every group: a critical reading anywhere in the set pulls the cycle to it. | A plain turn stays inside a group only when the dial has a gesture that can switch groups. Legacy has none, so on Legacy a plain turn, the auto cycle and the overviews treat all groups as one list, in group order. A Sensor Control group jump still lands in the next group, but turns then keep stepping through that one list, past the group’s last reading into the following group. On Custom, assign Switch sensor or group to a turn and the boundaries engage; assign it nowhere and the dial keeps one flat list, so no group can become unreachable. | The Sensor Control key’s Next sensor or group and Previous sensor or group honor your groups on every preset. | A single group behaves like a plain rotation set. A stats reset clears set to The whole rotation set means every group. | .

19.title: Touch zones
19.content: Off by default, and only on Elite and Custom: the Touch zones select appears for those presets, and Legacy always treats the strip as one tap. | Touch zones | What a tap does | . | Off (the whole strip is one tap) | The tap command, anywhere on the dial’s segment | . | Two: left and right switch readings | Left half: previous reading. Right half: next reading | . | Three: left and right switch, center taps | Left third: previous reading. Center third: the tap command. Right third: next reading | . The tap command is Touch tap on Custom and stat cycling on Elite. With two zones it never fires. Zone edges sit at exact halves or thirds of the dial’s 200 pixel wide touch segment; a tap exactly on a boundary counts as the zone to its right. A long touch runs its own command wherever you touch. Zone steps still work with Ignore turns on; a pinned dial does not move.

20.title: Pause, pin, and reset reach
20.content: . | Pause/resume auto cycle stops the auto cycle until you resume it. Resuming waits one full interval before the next step. While an auto cycle is set, the dial shows cycle paused where it normally says session. | Pin/unpin this reading locks the selection: turns, touch-zone steps, the auto cycle and Sensor Control selection commands cannot move the dial off its reading until you unpin. Stat cycling, resets and pause still work from a push, a touch or a Sensor Control key. A turn does nothing while the dial is pinned or Ignore turns is on, even a turn set to Cycle stat mode on Custom. The dial shows pinned where it normally says session. | A stats reset clears chooses what a reset clears: This reading only (default), The whole rotation set, or Every dial, everywhere (use with care). Every dial, everywhere includes dials parked on other pages and profiles. No default gesture uses it; you have to pick it on purpose. After a reset the dial says stats reset, set stats reset or all dials reset for a moment. | . Pause and pin survive page switches and profile changes for up to 30 minutes off screen; the plugin keeps the state of the 64 most recently hidden dials, and past either limit a returning dial starts fresh. They are kept in memory only, so they reset when the plugin restarts, for example when the Stream Deck app restarts.

21.title: Session stats are per reading
21.content: Each reading keeps its own local session min, max and average, and ordinary rotation keeps that session. These sessions are separate from the MIN, MAX and AVG on Sensor Reading keys, which no dial gesture or Sensor Control key resets. See session statistics for the full rules and how a dial’s statistics can differ from a key’s.

22.title: Thresholds and mixed units
22.content: A reading is warning once it crosses Warn at and critical once it crosses Critical at, in the alert direction: at or above the value by default, at or below it with Alert when the value drops to or below these numbers. A key turns its whole face amber or red. A dial keeps its theme: in the one-reading view only the range bar’s fill takes the alert color, and in the overviews, which have no bar, the alerting row’s own value takes it. Warn at, Critical at and the manual bar range apply only to readings measured in the unit they were configured against. Type a warn value of 80 while a °C reading is on the dial, and it never fires on a fan at 3000 RPM you rotate to. Edit a threshold or a bar end and the plugin anchors them to the unit of the reading on the dial at that moment. A threshold saved without a unit anchor applies to every reading until the next edit anchors it. Alert-aware cycling is opt-in, with Auto cycle jumps to a critical reading in the rotation and holds there while it stays critical under Alerts. Ticked, the auto cycle never rotates away from a reading that is currently critical, and its next step goes to a critical member of your set instead of the next one in order. A manual turn still moves away. Unticked (the default), alerts do not steer the cycle; it keeps stepping in order, straight through critical readings. See Thresholds and alerts.

23.title: The Sensor Control key action
23.content: Sensor Control is a key action that steers Sensor Dials from another key: a plain key, a pedal, a G-key or a Multi Action step, on this or another Stream Deck. The command carries its own target, so the key’s own device does not matter. Pedals and G-keys have not been checked on hardware. Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel on a simulated host with sample readings and Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. It is not the Stream Deck app’s own window. Pick a command under When pressed: . | Command | What the matching dials do | . | Next reading (default) / Previous reading | Step one reading in the rotation, as a turn would | . | Next sensor or group / Previous sensor or group | Jump to the next or previous rotation group; without groups, to the next or previous sensor group | . | Cycle stat mode | Current, MIN, MAX, AVG, then current again | . | Show current value, Show session min, Show session max, Show session average | Show that value directly | . | Pause auto cycle / Resume auto cycle / Pause/resume auto cycle | Pause, resume, or toggle | . | Pin reading / Unpin reading / Pin/unpin reading | Pin, unpin, or toggle | . | Reset session stats | Clear session statistics, as far as A reset clears reaches | . The panel’s header restates the choice in words, for example Reset session stats, current reading over Sends to dials with Link ID “cpu”. The reset command reveals A reset clears: The dial’s current reading (default), The dial’s rotation set, or Every dial, everywhere (use with care). The last one ignores the Target and clears session stats on all dials on all Stream Decks, including hidden ones; the header then says it sends to every dial on every Stream Deck. Targeting is explicit. Give a dial a Link ID (in its Controls section) and put the same name in the Sensor Control key’s Target field; the key then drives only dials with that ID, wherever they are. Spaces at either end are ignored, and the rest must match exactly. An empty Target drives every dial. | The command fires when you release the key, once per press, under the settings the press started with. Changing the key’s settings while it is held cancels that press. | For a moment after the release, the key shows its icon with a small tick when the command reached at least one matching dial (a pinned dial still counts as reached), and the Stream Deck alert triangle when none matched. A command this version does not know also shows the alert triangle. | The four selection commands (next and previous reading, next and previous sensor or group) need the target dial on screen on a connected deck. They work with Ignore turns on, but not on a pinned dial or one whose saved reading is missing. | The stat, pause, pin and reset commands also reach a dial parked off screen inside the same 30-minute window that keeps its pause and pin. The tick means the command matched a dial, not that anything changed on screen. | Pause and pin have one-way commands, so repeating Pause auto cycle in a Multi Action does not toggle the state back. | . The panel’s Advanced section holds Copy support report. A Sensor Control key changes only the plugin’s display and local session state; it does not control hardware or fans.

24.title: Page swipe
24.content: Swiping sideways on the touch strip switches Stream Deck pages. The Stream Deck app handles that gesture; the plugin only keeps state across it. The reading on the dial and its labels are saved settings. Pause and pin are kept off screen within the hidden-dial limits above. A swipe that shows a Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile again within 2 seconds keeps every session (When reading starts and stops). Page swipe has not been checked on a physical Stream Deck + yet; see Page swipe and page changes. If a gesture does nothing, see Dial gestures do nothing; the dial’s own screens are on Status screens.

25.title: Stored settings
25.content: These rules decide how a dial reads what is stored in its settings, whoever wrote them. | A dial without a controlPreset value, or with a value this version does not know, runs Legacy. | On Custom, a gesture with no valid command uses its Legacy command. | Touch zones other than the exact two- or three-zone values mean off. | Rotation groups are optional. Fewer than two groups that hold readings means no groups, and the flat rotation set drives the dial. The panel keeps the flat set equal to all grouped readings. | The threshold unit anchor (alertUnit) is written by the plugin when you edit a threshold or bar end, from the reading on screen at that moment. Until then a threshold applies to every reading. | The dial’s View (dialView) switches face only on its exact markers, overview and tworow. Anything else draws the one-reading face. | Per-reading names (rotationNames) are written only by Rename. An entry that is empty, blank or not text is ignored. | Row labels (overviewLabels) shortens shared words unless it is exactly full. Context line moves below the rows only on exactly bottom; Separators hide only on exactly off. | An Auto cycle value that is a positive whole number of milliseconds runs at that interval, even one the menu does not offer; the panel then shows it as, for example, Every 90 s (not in this list, kept). Any other value means off. | Malformed or unexpected values in any field fall back to the defaults instead of failing, so a damaged settings document still renders. | The settings panel keeps what it does not understand. Opening a panel writes nothing. An edit writes only the settings that control owns: choosing Custom after Elite also fills the gestures you have not set, editing a threshold or bar end also stores its unit anchor, a rotation edit also updates the flat rotation set beside the groups, and Make shared writes the shared theme and sets this dial back to Default. A stored choice this version does not offer shows as Stored value “…” (not in this list, kept) until you pick another. | .

27.title: Dial controls and presets
27.content: Choose what turning, pressing and touching a Sensor Dial does. Open its Controls section for Gestures, Touch zones, Ignore turns, Auto cycle, A stats reset clears and Link ID. Rotation groups are under Reading. Thresholds and Auto cycle jumps to a critical reading are under Alerts. Dial gestures have not yet been run on a physical Stream Deck +. Everything on this page is what the code implements and its tests check, including synthetic gesture traces replayed through the production gesture code. See Hardware compatibility.

29.title: Does it work on other operating systems?
29.content: No. Mac Sensors runs only on macOS. Its manifest declares macOS as the only platform, and the package carries native readers for Apple silicon (arm64) and Intel (x86_64) Mac computers only.

30.title: What are the exact requirements?
30.content: . | macOS 13.5 or later | Stream Deck app 7.1 or later, with the Node 24 runtime the app supplies | Tahoma Bold, which ships with macOS (Tahoma Bold prerequisite). | . These are declared floors. Measured: Apple silicon M5 Pro, macOS 27.0.1, Stream Deck app 7.5.0 and 7.6.0 on the Virtual Stream Deck. Physical Stream Deck key checks and Stream Deck + dial gestures are pending. See Hardware compatibility and Installation. Sensor Reading goes on keys. Sensor Dial needs a deck with dials, such as Stream Deck + or Stream Deck + XL.

31.title: Is Mac Sensors affiliated with Apple or Elgato?
31.content: No. Mac Sensors is an independent project by Stephen Lawrensen, free and MIT licensed, with no ads. It is not affiliated with Apple or Elgato. Mac and macOS are trademarks of Apple Inc. Stream Deck is a trademark of Corsair Memory, Inc.

32.title: Do I need a separate sensor app?
32.content: No. The plugin reads macOS system counters and SMC readings itself, through the native reader in its package. It installs no separate monitoring app, privileged helper or daemon. There is also no data source to choose: each read covers the system counters and the SMC readings together. See Data sources.

34.title: Which Mac models and readings are supported?
34.content: Available readings depend on the Mac model and macOS version. A reading appears only when this Mac answers for it with a valid value. On the measured Mac17,9 with an M5 Pro, the catalog has 38 SMC readings (temperatures, fans, power and related values) and 14 system readings: CPU usage, memory counters, swap, startup volume space, and network and storage transfer rates. Other models get a common table of typed SMC readings; the M5-specific table applies only to the measured model, and the plugin log notes that the model’s own catalog is not qualified. CPU and GPU clock speeds and GPU usage are not offered. Hardware compatibility lists what was measured. Data sources explains what each reading means.

35.title: Does it run on Intel Mac computers or under Rosetta?
35.content: The package carries a separate x86_64 reader, and the plugin loads it whenever its Node runtime is x86_64. Hosted Intel virtual machines with an emulated SMC have loaded it and read values; physical Intel validation is in progress (Hardware compatibility). On Apple silicon the plugin loads its arm64 reader when the Stream Deck app’s Node runtime is arm64. Every Node runtime the Stream Deck app supplied on the measured M5 Pro is an arm64-only file, so it does not run under Rosetta. When Node runs as x86_64 under Rosetta, the plugin loads the x86_64 reader and the support report’s translation field says translated. Outside the Stream Deck app, x86_64 Node 20, 22 and 24 running under Rosetta loaded that reader and read live values on the M5 Pro. The Stream Deck app itself has not been run under Rosetta, and Rosetta results are not Intel results. See Hardware compatibility.

36.title: Why is a reading missing?
36.content: The key shows Sensor missing / pick again when its saved reading is not in the current catalog on this Mac. This Mac may not offer that reading, its last read may have failed, or its value may have expired: a failed reading is removed at once, and no value is shown more than 15 seconds after it was acquired. The saved selection, label and colors stay. When the same reading returns, the key shows it again. The plugin never substitutes the nearest name or list position. See Status screens. If values are shown but do not seem to change, see Values do not seem to update.

38.title: How are MIN, MAX and AVG calculated on a key?
38.content: macOS reports current values only, so Mac Sensors keeps its own statistics for every reading. MIN and MAX are the lowest and highest value accepted for the reading since the plugin last started reading sensors, and AVG is the arithmetic mean of those reads: one sample per read, including a read that repeats the last value, not weighted by time. Changing pages, opening sensor details and pressing Back keep them (When reading starts and stops). The statistics belong to the reading, so every key and detail tile that shows it shows the same numbers. They start over after a gap in that reading (a read where it is missing, withheld or failed, or the reading expiring 15 seconds after its last read), when its unit or type changes, and when the plugin stops reading sensors (2 seconds after the last one disappears) or restarts. After a sleep, CPU usage and the transfer rates skip one read, so theirs start over. Changing Read every keeps them. A key has no command that resets them. The full rules are under Value shown. Alerts keep checking the current value whatever Value shown says.

39.title: How do dial session statistics differ?
39.content: A Sensor Dial keeps its own minimum, maximum and average for each reading, from the observations it accepted since the session started. Each new acquisition counts once, including one with an unchanged value; drawing the same acquisition again does not count. Each reading in a rotation keeps its own session, so turning away and back shows that reading’s numbers. A session starts over when you reset it, when the reading goes missing, when its unit or type changes, or when a status screen replaces the readings. After a status screen, the first live frame shows stats reset: data gap. Sessions live in the plugin’s memory only. A dial and a key showing the same reading can therefore show different numbers. A key’s statistics cover every read since the plugin started reading sensors. A dial counts only the reads made while it follows the reading (the reading on the dial, its rotation set or an overview’s list), from when it first followed it or was last reset, and any status screen ends its sessions. See Sensor Dial.

41.title: Why does a sparkline start empty and fill in?
41.content: The plugin keeps the last 36 samples of each graphed reading in memory and adds one per read while a Sensor Reading key (including the Back tile of a detail page), Sensor Dial or detail tile is visible. Every new acquisition is a sample, including one with an unchanged value. At the default Read every of 1 second, 36 samples take about 36 seconds; at 250 ms about 9 seconds; at 5 seconds about 3 minutes. The line draws from the second sample and always spans the full graph width, so an early line is coarse and gains detail as samples arrive. Samples are spaced by count, not by time. CPU usage and transfer rates need two reads before they have a value; the second read runs about a quarter second after reading starts. The line clears and starts again when: . | Read every changes (Advanced, Connection). | A status screen replaces the readings, for example Reading sensors or No sensor data. | The reading goes missing or has no valid value, or its unit or type changes. | No Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile has been visible anywhere for 2 seconds, which stops reading. A page change, opening sensor details or pressing Back inside those 2 seconds keeps the line. | The plugin restarts. | . Switching °F on or off does not clear it: samples are stored in the reading’s own unit.

43.title: How much CPU and memory does it use?
43.content: PERF.md in the product repository records each measurement with its build, host and harness; that repository requires access. The figures below are for an earlier 1.0.1 candidate, built before key statistics and the 2 second hold, run as a development copy in the Stream Deck app 7.5.0 on the M5 Pro (macOS 27.0.1), with 32 single-reading keys on an 8 by 4 Virtual Stream Deck. The harness was the development process observer, sampling the plugin process every 5 seconds in back-to-back runs against 1.0.0. CPU is the mean of two runs; RSS is the maximum of each run. | Read every | Plugin CPU, one core | Maximum RSS | . | 1 second (default) | 0.668% | 88.2 and 89.3 MiB | . | 250 ms | 2.478% | 95.9 and 94.6 MiB | . A 24-hour observation of the published 1.0.1.0, run as a development copy in the Stream Deck app 7.6.0 with 32 single-reading keys at 1 second, used 0.704% of one core, peaked at 92.55 MiB of RSS and closed at 50.41 MiB while the Mac was under memory pressure. It kept 12 threads and 49 to 50 file descriptors and logged no warnings or errors. Limits: one build’s CPU differed by 35% between two sessions in the same harness, other development work ran during the measurements, and dials, detail views and keys that mix system and SMC readings were not measured in the app. These are recorded results on one Mac, not a promise for another.

44.title: What does Read every change?
44.content: Read every (Advanced, Connection) sets how often the one shared read runs for every key and dial: 250 ms, 500 ms, 1 second (the default), 2 seconds or 5 seconds. Shorter intervals update sooner and use more processor time: in the table above, 250 ms used about 3.7 times the CPU of 1 second. An earlier 1.0.1 candidate in the same harness used 0.44% of one core at 2 seconds and 0.21% at 5 seconds. Changing Read every clears sparkline history and keeps every MIN, MAX and AVG. A blank value means 1 second, and a stored value outside 250 ms to 5 seconds runs at the nearest limit.

45.title: Does adding keys add more sensor reads?
45.content: No. One shared read per interval serves every visible Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial and detail tile, however many there are. Each extra key adds drawing work and messages to the Stream Deck app, not another read. When none of them is visible anywhere, the plugin makes no new reads, and 2 seconds later reading stops until one appears; Sensor Control keys do not keep it running. With nothing visible, the plugin process keeps running and keeps its connection to the Stream Deck app. In the measured show and hide cycles it made no reads, ticks or frames while hidden; those cycles ran on a build without the 2 second hold, and this is not a measurement of idle CPU. See When reading starts and stops. A key can show up to four readings (Readings on this key), a dial can turn through a set of readings, and a key can open a detail page, so a deck can show more readings than it has keys. The measured bench above used 32 keys.

46.title: Can several keys show the same reading?
46.content: Yes. Each key keeps its own Label on the key, layout, theme, Text color, Decimals, °F, Value shown, Graph under the value and alert thresholds. They all use the same shared read, draw the same sparkline history for that reading and show the same MIN, MAX and AVG.

48.title: Why is a key amber or red?
48.content: The current value reached a threshold set under Alerts in that key’s settings: . | At or past Warn at, the whole key turns amber with dark text. | At or past Critical at, it turns red with white text. | . By default a higher value is worse. Tick Alert when the value drops to or below these numbers where low is the problem, such as fan speed. Alerts check the current value in the reading’s own unit (°F when °F is on), even when Value shown names a statistic; for bytes and rates they check the source’s number and unit, which the key may show rescaled. On a key with several readings, only reading 1 is checked, and it recolors the whole key. With Graph under the value set to Bar or Ring, muted amber and red zones mark the thresholds on the track whenever they are set, crossed or not. A zone marks where a threshold sits; the alert is the key’s color change. On a dial the face keeps its theme: the bar takes the alert color, or in an overview the row’s value does. Once thresholds are set, the one-reading bar’s track also marks the warning and critical zones in muted amber and red. Dial thresholds apply only to readings in the unit that was on the dial when you last changed them. Alert colors are the same in every theme. To turn alerts off, clear Warn at and Critical at. How the colors look on a physical deck has not been checked yet. See Thresholds and alerts.

49.title: How do I reset a dial’s session statistics?
49.content: . | Legacy (the default): push the dial. | Elite: hold the push for at least half a second. | Custom: assign Reset session stats to Short push, Long push, Touch tap or Long touch. | . A stats reset clears (under Controls) sets the scope: This reading only, The whole rotation set or Every dial, everywhere (use with care). A Sensor Control key set to Reset session stats sends the same command from any key, pedal or Multi Action, with its own A reset clears. The next accepted observation starts the new session. A Sensor Reading key has no reset: its MIN, MAX and AVG start over only as How are MIN, MAX and AVG calculated on a key? describes. See Dial controls and presets.

51.title: Why isn’t Default the same as Void?
51.content: Default is a link. A key or dial set to Default follows the shared theme under Advanced, Shared defaults, Theme, which every Mac Sensors key and dial set to Default uses. On a fresh install the shared theme is Void, so Default draws Void until you change it. Picking the Void chip instead keeps that key on Void when the shared theme changes. In the theme strip the Default chip has a dashed frame and a link mark. The line above the chips names what is drawn: Default (shared: Void) follows the shared theme; Void (set on this key) is the key’s own pick. If the plugin finds saved settings but no shared theme the first time an action appears, it starts the shared theme on Graphite instead of Void.

52.title: Why doesn’t a key follow my shared theme?
52.content: A theme picked on the key wins. Changing the shared theme affects only keys and dials set to Default. Pick the Default chip on that key to make it follow again, or choose Make shared to make the key’s theme the shared one and set the key back to Default. See Themes and colors.

53.title: Can I choose another font?
53.content: No. Faces use Tahoma Bold, and the panel shows Text font: Tahoma Bold. A font choice saved in a configuration document stays in the document and is not used.

55.title: Is my data sent anywhere? Any telemetry?
55.content: No. The plugin makes no internet requests and has no telemetry or ads. It reads macOS interfaces and SMC readings on this Mac and draws the faces locally. Its only connection is the Stream Deck SDK’s WebSocket to the Stream Deck app at the loopback address 127.0.0.1. Settings are stored by the Stream Deck app, and logs stay on this Mac. The only web address in the settings panel is a link to this documentation.

56.title: What is in a support report?
56.content: Copy support report (Advanced, Support) builds a report on this Mac and copies it to the clipboard. Nothing is uploaded; it goes only where you paste it. It contains the plugin, Stream Deck app and macOS versions, the Node runtime version and architecture, the Mac model and chip, whether the plugin runs translated, the number of readings and any error codes from each source, the read interval and state, Stream Deck device models with hashed identifiers, and recent events. It leaves out user names, serial numbers, hardware UUIDs, raw device identifiers and sensor values. Review a report before you share it. Event tracing is a development switch that is off unless set, and writes only to local logs. See Copy a support report.

57.title: Is the native reader signed? How do I verify what I installed?
57.content: The two native reader files, bin/hwmac-arm64.node and bin/hwmac-x86_64.node, are ad-hoc signed. An ad-hoc signature checks that a file is intact. It is not a Developer ID certificate, and the files are not notarized. Before it loads a reader, the plugin checks the file’s SHA-256 against the list in its own package and checks its architecture and protocol; a mismatch shows Bridge failed. Check the package as described in Check the download. To check the installed readers, compare the hashes the commands below print with the sha256 entries in the same release’s native-manifest.json, then inspect the signature: . cd ~/Library/Application\ Support/com.elgato.StreamDeck/Plugins/com.lawrensen.mac.sdPlugin/bin shasum -a 256 hwmac-arm64.node hwmac-x86_64.node codesign --verify --strict hwmac-arm64.node codesign -dv --verbose=4 hwmac-arm64.node . The last command reports Signature=adhoc. A checksum identifies bytes; it does not establish that a file is safe.

59.title: Does it need administrator access, a helper or a kernel extension?
59.content: No. Mac Sensors installs no privileged helper, launch daemon or kernel extension and needs no root or administrator password for normal reads. On the measured Mac, installing it showed no prompt beyond the Stream Deck app’s own install confirmation.

60.title: Can it change fan speeds or write SMC values?
60.content: No. The reader is read-only. Its SMC path accepts only read and key-metadata requests and rejects every other request code before it reaches the SMC; a test sends all 256 codes to confirm it. There is no fan control or other setter. Alerts change only what the plugin draws.

62.title: Do keys survive restarts and sensor changes?
62.content: Yes. A key saves the identity of its measurement, not a list position or label. A system reading is saved by its counter name, such as CPU usage. An SMC reading is saved by the Mac model, its four SMC key bytes and a meaning revision. That identity does not depend on catalog order, labels or build numbers, so a new order after a restart cannot point a saved key at a different reading. A custom label changes only what the key shows. If the saved reading is absent, the key shows Sensor missing / pick again and keeps its settings. When the same identity returns, the key shows it again.

63.title: Can I move settings to another Mac?
63.content: Yes, through configuration documents. Under Advanced, Configuration documents, Copy puts this key’s settings or the shared settings on the clipboard as JSON. On the other Mac, paste it into the same box and choose Replace this key’s settings or Replace shared settings. Replacing shared settings changes every Mac Sensors key and dial and asks for a second click. Fields this version does not know stay in the document. System readings use the same identity on every Mac. An SMC reading’s identity includes the Mac model, so on a different model that reading shows Sensor missing until you pick one there. Nothing is rebound automatically.

64.title: What happens when my Mac sleeps?
64.content: After a sleep longer than 15 seconds, keys and dials can show No sensor data until the first read after waking returns, because every reading is older than its 15-second limit. After any sleep, CPU usage and transfer rates return one Read every interval later. This comes from the code and its software tests; real sleep and wake with a deck attached has not been checked yet. See Sleep and wake.

65.title: What do the two-line screens on my keys mean?
65.content: They name the condition the plugin can establish and the next step: for example Reading sensors before the first sample, Sensor missing for a saved reading this Mac does not offer now, Tahoma needed when the font is not installed, and Bridge failed when the native reader cannot load. The saved selection stays through every one of them, so there is no need to delete and rebuild a key. See Status screens for each screen and Troubleshooting for what to do.

66.title: How do updates arrive?
66.content: Open a newer .streamDeckPlugin package. The plugin has no update channel of its own and downloads nothing. Packages come from the project’s GitHub releases, which require repository access. Mac Sensors is not on the Elgato Marketplace yet. Opening a package with the same version as the installed one does nothing; see Opening the same version again does nothing.

68.title: Where do I report a bug or a security issue?
68.content: Report a bug as a public issue on the documentation repository. Name Mac Sensors and its version, the status on the key, and where you got the package; a reviewed support report helps. Report a suspected vulnerability through the private security-report form, naming Mac Sensors and the affected version. Do not post exploit details, profile exports or private logs in a public issue. The first reply target for a security report is seven days.

69.content: For a screen on a key or dial, start with Status screens, then Troubleshooting. To set up a first key, see Getting started. For what each reading means, see Data sources, and for what was measured, Hardware compatibility.

70.content: For a status on a key or dial, see Status screens and Troubleshooting. For changes by version, see the changelog.

71.title: 1. Install the plugin
71.content: In Finder, double-click com.lawrensen.mac.streamDeckPlugin and choose Install when the Stream Deck app asks. The actions list gains a Mac Sensors category. Version 1.0.1.0 is published as a GitHub release that requires repository access; Mac Sensors is not on the Elgato Marketplace yet. Installation covers getting, checking, updating and removing the package.

72.title: 2. Confirm Tahoma Bold
72.content: Open Font Book and search for Tahoma. Tahoma Bold should be listed and turned on. Without it, every Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial and detail tile shows Tahoma needed and Open Font Book, and no readings appear. Install Tahoma Bold in Font Book, then choose Check again in the key’s settings. The Tahoma Bold prerequisite explains how the plugin checks for it.

73.title: 3. Add Sensor Reading
73.content: In Stream Deck, drag Mac Sensors → Sensor Reading onto an empty key. Select the key to open its settings. Until the first read completes, the key shows Reading sensors. Then it shows Pick a sensor and in settings, and the settings header says No reading selected and Mac sensors ready. Sensor Dial works the same way on a dial of a Stream Deck + or + XL. The Virtual Stream Deck has no dials.

74.title: 4. Select a reading
74.content: Click Reading, type part of a reading or group name such as cpu super or fan, and choose a result. The list groups readings under CPU, GPU, Memory, Storage, Network, Battery, Fans and System, as far as this Mac reports them. Arrow keys browse, Return picks, and Tab or a click elsewhere closes the list without changing anything. The button beside the box, Reload the sensor list, asks the plugin for the list again. Opening the panel saves nothing. Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel on a simulated host with sample readings and Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. It is not the Stream Deck app’s own window.

75.title: 5. Confirm a value
75.content: The key shows a number and unit, and the settings header shows Live · Mac sensors. Readings update once per Read every interval, set under Advanced, Connection: 1 second by default, from 250 ms to 5 seconds. CPU usage and transfer rates need two reads, so they appear about a quarter second after reading starts (When reading starts and stops). Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel in a simulated host with sample data, with Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere, so the header face’s sparkline uses the theme accent. It is not the Stream Deck app’s own window. A press cycles current, min, max and avg. Mac Sensors keeps min, max and avg for each reading from its reads since the plugin last started reading sensors, and they start over after a gap in that reading (Value shown). Dials keep their own local session statistics. If you see Tahoma needed, Reading sensors, No sensor data, Sensor missing or Bridge failed, find the exact message in Status screens or Troubleshooting.

82.title: Sensor details support
82.content: The sensor detail view ships one bundled page per deck type: Mini (3 by 2), 15-key (5 by 3), Neo (4 by 2), + (4 by 2 keys), XL (8 by 4) and + XL (9 by 4 keys). Back is the top-left key on every page. The Mini page has no title tile; on the XL and + XL pages Back, title, Previous and Next run down the left column. The Virtual Stream Deck borrows the page with the most reading tiles whose key grid fits its size, from every page except the + page; a virtual deck at least 9 keys wide and 4 keys high runs the + XL page. The first time details open on each kind of deck, Stream Deck asks to install the bundled detail view, and asks again after an update that changes it. The bundled pages are checked by archive tests and by a mock-host detail run on the 15-key page. The detail view and Back on a physical deck are pending. Decks without a bundled page (Mobile, Studio, Galleon, Corsair Voyager, Pedal, G-Keys, and a Virtual Stream Deck too small for the 3 by 2 Mini page) do not open details: the key shows the Stream Deck alert triangle and the deck stays on its page.

83.title: Page swipe and page changes
83.content: On a Stream Deck +, a sideways swipe on the touch strip changes pages. The Stream Deck app handles the swipe. Readings, labels and colors are saved settings, so they come back with the page. A hidden dial keeps its pause and pin for up to 30 minutes, and its session statistics for as long as reading continues; the plugin keeps the state of the 64 most recently hidden dials (Pause, pin, and reset reach). While a Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile stays visible anywhere, the plugin keeps reading and the hidden dial keeps adding to its session statistics. The Stream Deck app removes the old page’s actions before it shows the new page’s, so a page change leaves a moment with nothing visible. Reading continues for 2 seconds, so a page change keeps key MIN, MAX and AVG, sparklines, CPU usage, the rates and dial sessions. After 2 seconds with no Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile visible, reading stops, sparkline history is cleared and every reading’s MIN, MAX and AVG end. When a page with one returns after that, keys show Reading sensors until the first read, and CPU usage and transfer rates appear about a quarter second later. A dial that returns this way starts a new session and says stats reset: data gap once live data arrives. See When reading starts and stops. Physical swipes are pending; this behavior comes from the code and its software tests.

85.title: Event recorder
85.content: For development, the plugin has an event recorder. It is off by default. With MACSENSORS_TRACE_EVENTS=1 in the plugin process environment, the plugin appends one JSON line per dial input, dial appearance and disappearance, dial reading change, Sensor Control command, dial redraw and source observation to logs/trace-<pid>.jsonl in the plugin folder, and its log says the recorder is on. The trace is redacted where it is written: device IDs and reading identities are hashed, and no sensor values, sensor names, computer names or user paths are recorded. Its field names match the replay fixtures in the plugin’s tests, so a capture from real hardware can replace a synthetic trace. A tested way to start the Stream Deck app with that variable on macOS has not been recorded, so the procedure above uses the support report, which always carries the most recent events.

86.title: Support report
86.content: Copy support report is under Advanced, Support on a Sensor Reading key or a Sensor Dial, and under Advanced on a Sensor Control key. It builds a local JSON summary, including whether the event recorder is on, and copies it to the clipboard. Copy a support report lists the main parts of the report. It contains no sensor values or reading names, and the Node path shows your home folder as ~. Nothing is uploaded: the plugin makes no internet requests, and its only connection is the local link to the Stream Deck app. Detail view tiles have no settings of their own and no report button. Review the report before you post it.

102.title: Check the download
102.content: Each GitHub release includes SHA256SUMS.txt. Put the package, native-manifest.json and SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release in one folder and run: . shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt . Each line must end in OK. A matching checksum identifies the published bytes. It does not establish safety. The two native readers are ad-hoc signed: that checks file integrity, and it is not a Developer ID certificate or notarization. To inspect an extracted reader, run codesign --verify --strict <file> and codesign -dv --verbose=4 <file>. Before loading a reader, the plugin compares the file’s SHA-256 with the record inside the package. A file that does not match is not loaded, and keys show Bridge failed. Quit and reopen Stream Deck. If it persists, remove Mac Sensors and install it again (Removing).

107.title: Tahoma Bold prerequisite

When the font is missing, every Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial and detail tile shows a fixed setup image, Tahoma needed and Open Font Book, and readings are withheld until the font is back. Sensor Control keys keep their own image. The setup image is stored as pixels, so it draws without the font. 111.title: What it is (and is not)
111.content: The detail view is a plugin-managed profile, not a Stream Deck folder. A plugin cannot place keys inside your folders or profiles, so Mac Sensors ships one editable, one-page profile per supported deck type, named Mac Sensors Details in the app’s profile list, and switches to it when you press the opener. Pressing Back asks the Stream Deck app to return to the profile you came from. | The first time you open details on a deck type, the Stream Deck app asks to install that deck’s detail profile. Accept once; later entries switch without asking. If the install is declined, or not accepted within 30 seconds, that entry lapses and the next press tries again. If you accept later, up to 10 minutes after the entry lapsed, the plugin switches the deck back to the profile you came from. Press the opener again to open details. | The page is a normal, editable profile, but it ships with every cell filled: the Back tile, the title, the pagers and the reading tiles. Adding a key of your own means replacing one of those. The plugin never repairs or overwrites what you change. The shipped page holds no sensor choice of yours: every tile asks the plugin what to show while it is open. | What you change on that page is shared. There is one detail page per deck type, so a key you add or a tile you replace appears on every detail page you open on that deck, whichever key you pressed. What still follows the key you pressed is the live content: the reading tiles, the title, the page range and, until you pick a reading for it, the Back tile’s face. | The plugin has no reset for the page, because a plugin cannot edit a profile you already have installed. Whether removing the Mac Sensors Details profile in the Stream Deck app brings the install prompt back on the next detail entry has not been checked. | If you want a page you lay out yourself, with your own multi-reading keys on it, use a Stream Deck folder instead. That is the app’s own feature, and unlike the detail page it belongs to one key. A folder’s opener key shows a static icon; a detail opener shows a live reading. | The Stream Deck app never updates a profile that is already installed. When a plugin update changes the page itself, the change ships as a new profile revision with a new internal identity, the next detail entry asks once to install it, and the copy you already have stays in your profile list untouched. | Back asks the app for its previous profile; the plugin stores no profile history of its own, so where Back lands after a Stream Deck app restart is unknown. | Opening details and pressing Back do not restart reading. MIN, MAX and AVG, sparklines, CPU usage and the rates carry on, and keys show readings at once (When reading starts and stops). | .
