113.title: Choosing the list
113.content: Every reading from this reading’s sensor lists the other readings in the opener’s sensor group (CPU, GPU, Memory, Storage, Network, Battery, Fans or System), in the order the reading picker lists them. The opener’s own reading appears on Back and is left out of the list and its count. The list follows what this Mac reports: readings that appear or disappear change it while the page is open. A custom list uses the readings and the order you choose, with individual tile sizes, labels and colors. Add readings with the Add readings search under Details list: Tick readings to add or remove them. A listed reading that is the opener’s own reading is not given a tile, because the Back tile shows it; the editor marks it (Back tile). A listed reading this Mac does not report right now keeps its place, and its tile shows Sensor missing. The list holds up to 128 readings. Readings matching a filter matches the sensor group name and the reading label together, across every group. Matches update with each read. The panel shows a live count, such as Matches 12 readings right now., and the pattern becomes the page title unless you set Title tile text. See Filter patterns.

114.title: Editing custom tiles
114.content: The custom-list editor shows the list as the tiles the page will draw: . | Click a tile’s size to cycle it through 1, 2, 3 and 4 cells. Click a cell’s name to set its label on the tile; an empty label keeps the reading’s own name. On a full four-reading tile each cell has a color well for its identity color, and the Abc button switches to color-coded bare values (it then reads 123) and back. | Readings without a tile of your own follow Readings per tile. Resizing or shrinking such a tile saves it as a tile of your own. | The up and down arrows on a reading move it through the list; the drag handle on a tile moves the whole tile, and arrow keys move it too. Dragging a reading into another tile shrinks the tile it left and grows the one it lands in, at the spot marked by the blue caret. A full four-reading tile cannot take another cell; the reading becomes its own tile beside it. | Labels and colors move with the reading. Other readings keep theirs. If two readings end up with the same color, change one with its color well. | Removing a reading shrinks its tile; the next tile’s readings do not move up to fill it. Press a tile’s + to send the next readings you tick into that tile, up to four cells; the + after the last tile starts a new one. | . The note under the editor counts what the page lists, for example 7 readings across 3 tiles. Grouping is positional: readings flow through the tile sizes in list order, and readings past your groups follow Readings per tile.

115.title: The detail page
115.content: . Production-rendered sample data on the bundled 15-key detail layout, with a custom list and a blank title tile text, so the title reads Custom set. Long catalog labels are shortened the way the tile draws them. Every detail page has these controls: . | Back (always top left, where a folder’s back key sits): a real Sensor Reading key whose press is fixed to leaving the view; a small return arrow in the tile’s lower-left corner marks it. Fresh from the install it shows the reading you opened the page from, live, with that key’s theme, text color, units, decimals and thresholds. It stays pressable while sensor data is unavailable, while the reading is missing, and right after a plugin restart. | A second Back under your finger, on by default. When the opener key’s cell falls on a reading cell of the page, that cell becomes a second Back tile showing the same opener face with the return arrow, so you can go back without moving your hand. The readings flow around it; none are hidden, and it costs one tile per page. Untick Also go back from this key’s own position on the opener to keep only the top-left Back. | Title (every deck except the Mini): the sensor group name, the filter pattern, Custom set or your Title tile text, over the visible range, such as CPU over 1-11 / 18 (a CPU opener on the measured M5 Pro, on a 15-key deck with the second Back off). The range counts readings, not tiles. Pressing the title does nothing. | Previous and Next: page through long lists. A chevron dims at either end; paging does not wrap. Paging happens inside the one profile page; nothing stacks. | Reading tiles: live readings in the opener’s theme. At one reading per tile, each tile carries its own reading’s type accent; a denser tile carries its first reading’s accent. Pressing a tile cycles current, MIN, MAX and AVG for everything on it, for this visit; leaving the view resets that. On MIN, MAX or AVG a tile shows each reading’s statistics since the plugin last started reading sensors, the same numbers a Sensor Reading key shows for that reading. Reading tiles do not take the opener’s thresholds, because a temperature limit means nothing on a power or fan tile. The Back tile keeps its own. | No trend lines on reading tiles. A trend line needs history that fills over many reads, and a detail page shows many readings (up to 128 on a + XL at four per tile) that change with every page turn and filter. The opener key keeps its own graph on your page. | . If sensor data becomes unavailable while the page is open, the tiles show the same status screens as ordinary keys (Status screens) and recover on their own; Back keeps working throughout. If a listed reading disappears from a custom list, its tile shows Sensor missing in place, and the other tiles do not shift.

116.title: Configuring the Back tile
116.content: The Back tile is an ordinary Sensor Reading key with one fixed job. Select it in the Stream Deck app and its settings panel opens with everything a normal key has: the Reading picker, Label on the key, Readings on this key (one to four readings), the theme strip, Text color, Value shown, Decimals, °F, Graph under the value, and Warn at and Critical at. Its header reads Back tile · sensor detail view. Two things differ, and the panel says both: . | Pressing it always returns to the previous profile. A note under the header says so: This is the Back tile of the sensor detail view. Set its reading, layout and look like any key; pressing it always returns to the profile you came from, so press settings do not apply here. The Press section holds only a note in place of A press; press settings stored on the tile are kept, unused. The return arrow stays visible on every layout. | Until you pick a reading, the tile shows the reading you opened the page from, so a fresh page needs no setup. Once you pick one, the tile shows your pick, and a missing pick shows Sensor missing like any key would. | . Copying the Back tile elsewhere copies its fixed role too: a pasted copy still returns to the previous profile when pressed. For an ordinary key, add a new Sensor Reading from the actions list instead. The other cells (title, pagers and reading tiles) are Sensor Detail Slot actions, which do not appear in the actions list. Selecting one opens a panel that says the tile belongs to the plugin-managed sensor detail view and has no settings of its own. A tile whose role this version does not know, for example from a detail profile made by another version, says Unrecognized detail tile; it shows an empty face and does nothing when pressed. To change what the view lists, its title or its look, go back and select the Sensor Reading key that opened it.

117.title: Filter patterns
117.content: The filter is a glob, not a regular expression: * spans anything, ? matches exactly one character, everything else is literal, and case never matters. Every reading is tested against one text: the sensor group name, a single space, then the reading label. For the first fan that text is Fans Fan 1; for a memory reading it is Memory Memory free. That is why one pattern can select a whole group or a kind of reading across groups, and why an anchored pattern must allow for the group name at the front. Three rules cover it: . | Plain text matches anywhere. A pattern with no wildcard behaves as if wrapped in *...*, so fan and *fan* are the same filter. | One wildcard anchors the whole pattern. As soon as a pattern contains * or ?, the automatic wrapping is off and the pattern must cover the entire text. core* matches nothing, because the text starts with the group name, not with “core”; *core* is the form you want. | Spaces are literal. Multi-word plain text works only when the words sit next to each other: fan 1 finds Fans Fan 1, but cpu core finds nothing because the core readings are named like CPU super core 1. Span the gap with a star: *cpu*core*. | . Examples, by these rules: . | Pattern | What it gathers | . | fans | every reading in the Fans group | . | memory | every reading in the Memory group, plus any reading whose label contains Memory | . | storage* | every reading in the Storage group (the text starts with Storage) | . | network | the Network readings, such as Network receive and Network send | . | *total* | every reading whose group or label contains total, such as Memory total | . | *core* | per-core CPU temperatures, on a Mac whose catalog lists them | . | ?PU* | readings in groups whose name is one character plus PU: CPU and GPU (anchored start) | . | * | every reading, paged | . The Filter field’s sample text, *4090*, and the help’s example, *gpu*fan*, match no Mac reading. Start from a pattern in the table above. Which readings exist depends on the Mac model and macOS version, so a pattern’s matches differ from one Mac to another; the panel’s count shows what this Mac reports now. See Data sources. An empty pattern refuses entry with the Stream Deck alert triangle, and the panel says Type a pattern; the view refuses to open while it is empty. A pattern that matches nothing opens an empty view reading 0 / 0, and the panel warns Matches nothing right now; the view would open empty (0 / 0). Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed, and everything past 128 characters is cut. The panel’s live count reflects all of this before you press.

118.title: When a press does not open the page
118.content: A press that cannot open details keeps the key as it was, with no statistic cycled in its place, and shows the Stream Deck alert triangle: . | The deck has no bundled detail profile (see Supported decks). | The list cannot be built yet: Every reading from this reading’s sensor and Readings matching a filter need sensor data, and the sensor list also needs the opener’s own reading. A custom list opens even while sensor data is unavailable, as long as the key has a reading selected. | The filter pattern is empty. | The key has no Reading selected. Every Details list needs the key’s own reading, because it goes on the Back tile. | The detail page is already open on that deck, or the switch to it was sent moments ago. | . For the log line and the first-press install prompt, see Detail view problems.

119.title: Supported decks
119.content: One bundled profile per deck type. The layouts are generated from one table and checked by tests; reading tiles fill left to right, top to bottom around the navigation tiles. | Deck | Grid | Reading tiles per page | . | Stream Deck Mini | 3 by 2 | 3 (no title tile) | . | Stream Deck (15 keys) | 5 by 3 | 11 | . | Stream Deck Neo | 4 by 2 keys | 4 | . | Stream Deck + | 4 by 2 keys | 4 (the page puts no actions on the dials) | . | Stream Deck XL | 8 by 4 | 28 | . | Stream Deck + XL | 9 by 4 keys | 32 (the page puts no actions on the dials) | . | Virtual Stream Deck | your size | by fit (see below) | . Readings per tile multiplies those counts without changing the page: the tiles stay where they are and each carries up to four readings, so a + XL page lists up to 128 readings at once, and paging steps by readings, not tiles. The second Back, on by default, costs one tile per page. The Virtual Stream Deck’s grid is the size you gave it, so it borrows a layout instead of owning one: entry picks the layout with the most reading tiles that fits its grid. A 10 by 10 virtual deck runs the + XL layout (32 tiles per page; the page holds no dials), an 8 by 4 one the XL layout, a 5 by 3 one the 15-key layout, down to the Mini layout at 3 by 2. Below 3 by 2 there is no room for Back and the pagers, and entry refuses with the Stream Deck alert triangle. Stream Deck Mobile, Stream Deck Studio, Galleon 100 SD, Corsair Voyager, Stream Deck Pedal and G-keys have no bundled detail profile. A press set to open details shows the Stream Deck alert triangle instead of switching, and the Press section says Sensor details are not available on this deck, followed by the device in parentheses (Studio and Galleon 100 SD appear as an unknown device type). Everything else on the key keeps working. This does not establish support for the other actions on those devices; see Hardware compatibility. A pedal or G-key can carry a Sensor Control key instead; those devices have not been checked on hardware.

120.title: Privacy
120.content: Detail pages add no telemetry and no internet requests. The bundled profiles are static layout files that carry no sensor selection; your reading choices stay in the key’s own settings, which the Stream Deck app already saves and exports with your profiles.

121.title: Where to go next
121.content: . | Sensor Reading for the opener key and the Back tile’s own settings. | Detail view problems if a press does not open the page. | Sensor details support for what has been checked on which decks. | .

122.title: Sensor details
122.content: Press a Sensor Reading key to open related readings on a detail page. The key you pressed stays live on the page as a Back tile. Set it up: open the key’s Press section, choose Opens sensor details under A press, then choose a Details list. The first time details open on each kind of deck, Stream Deck asks to install the bundled detail view. Opening details, installing the detail profile and pressing Back have not yet been checked on a physical Stream Deck. What this page describes is what the code implements and its tests check. See Sensor details support.

123.title: The touchscreen readout
123.content: Each dial draws into its own 200 by 100 pixel segment of the touchscreen, filled with the theme’s background. The one-reading view draws four things, top to bottom: . | Element | Shows | . | Title | Your Title on the dial. Left blank, the name you gave the reading with Rename in the rotation list, else the reading’s own label. A title too wide for the segment is cut to fit. | . | Value and unit | The live reading, formatted by Decimals, with the unit inline. While you view a session statistic instead of the live value, a badge follows the unit: · MIN, · MAX or · AVG. Long text steps down to a smaller size so it stays inside the segment. | . | Stats line | ▼ <low> ▲ <high> session: the lowest and highest values this dial has observed for the reading in this session. Byte and rate readings pack it tighter, as ▼<low> ▲<high> session. pinned replaces session while the dial is pinned, and cycle paused while an auto cycle is set and paused. A line too long at 12 px draws at 11 px; a line too long even then leaves off session first, and only then is cut. | . | Range bar | A fill showing where the live value sits between the bar’s two ends, over the warn and critical zones when thresholds are set. | . The bar always follows the live value, even while the number above it shows MIN, MAX or AVG. A short message takes the whole stats line for about 1.6 seconds, then the line returns: . | Message | When | . | A group name, such as GPU or group 2 | A group jump landed in that group | . | stats reset, set stats reset, all dials reset | A reset cleared this reading, the rotation set, or every dial | . | cycle paused, cycle resumed | The auto cycle was paused or resumed | . | pinned, unpinned | The dial was pinned or unpinned | . | stats reset: data gap | The first live frame after sensor data was unavailable | . | stats reset: units changed, stats reset: reading changed | The reading on the dial changed its unit or its type, so its session started again | .

124.title: Views
124.content: View under Display offers the one-reading face and two multi-row layouts. Both multi-row layouts list what rotation moves through: . | Overview, two rows (big values and trend): two rows with large right-aligned values. The selected row sits on a band with an accent bar at its left edge. A long label wraps onto a second line; a row whose label fits on one line draws a trend line of its last 36 samples there when it has room. The footer shows the selected reading’s session low and high. | Overview, three rows: one line per reading. A thumb on the left rail marks the reading on the dial and where the visible window sits in the list. The context line carries the shared name, the state tags and the session ▼low ▲high; names shorten before statistics. Put it above or below the rows with Context line, and show or hide the lines between rows with Separators. A temporary message replaces the context line for its moment. | . Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel in a simulated host with sample data, showing the header and the Display section; the full capture opens from the image. Shared Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. Three things keep short labels readable: . | Shared words move to the context line. When the visible rows’ labels start with the same words, such as Memory free, Memory active and Memory wired, the shared part is shown once and the rows read free, active and wired. The three-row face puts Memory on the context line; the two-row face puts it at the end of its footer. Names you type yourself are never shortened, and a reading whose whole label is the shared words keeps it. To keep every label whole, set Row labels to Always full labels. | Values share one right-aligned column. Units sit in their own column beside it. The three-row face steps the value size down from 20 to 12 px until the widest visible value fits, and each row’s label runs up to its own value before it shortens. A wide rate unit in view moves the value and unit columns left together, so the unit is not cut at the screen edge. The two-row face places its columns by the widest visible value. | You can rename any reading in the rotation. Select it in the list under Readings to rotate through and press Rename in the toolbar under the list (or double-click it, or press F2 in the list). Type the new name in the Name on the dial for … field; Return or clicking away saves it, and an empty field goes back to the reading’s own name. The name shows on that reading’s row and as the dial’s title whenever that reading is on the dial, in every view. Removing the reading from the rotation keeps its name for later. | .

125.title: What the overview lists
125.content: The overview has no list of its own to manage. It shows what rotation already steps through, in the same order: . | your rotation set, if you built one (any size; the view shows a two- or three-row window of it), | the active rotation group, when rotation groups steer a plain turn, | otherwise the readings of the same sensor group as the reading on the dial, such as every CPU reading. | . Turning works as in the one-reading view: the selection steps through the whole list and is saved, the mark follows it, and the window scrolls with the selection, held at both ends. Auto cycle, alert interrupts, pin, pause, group jumps, touch taps and Sensor Control keys keep working. A touch tap through MIN, MAX and AVG switches every row to that statistic, each row from its own session, and the stat badge joins the state tags. Details specific to the overviews: . | The range bar and the big value belong to the one-reading view. Bar from and Bar to are hidden on the overviews and not used there; their values stay saved. | Warn at and Critical at still apply, scoped to their unit as always: a row whose live value crosses a threshold shows its value in the alert color, and the alert-aware auto cycle can pull the selection, and so the window, to it. | Title on the dial renames the marked row only, and it clears when the dial moves on to another reading unless Title when the dial moves on is Stays for this dial. Names given with Rename stay with each reading. | Values are cut at 12 characters, and every row uses this dial’s Decimals setting. Units are cut at 4 characters on the three-row face and 5 on the two-row face. | With fewer readings than rows, the overview lists what there is. The status faces are the same as the one-reading view’s. | . Switching back to One reading restores the one-reading face.

126.title: Reading colors
126.content: Choose one of the two overview View options under Display. Color numbers by sensor type and Reading colors then appear under the overview options. | Reading colors offers Automatic, Signal (four hues), Pairs (two hues) and Uniform. A preset colors the listed readings in order. When the colors match no preset, the select shows Custom. | Click a reading’s color well to give its number a color of its own. Two temperatures can have different colors. | Auto beside a reading resets that reading; Automatic resets every listed reading. A reading without a chosen color follows Color numbers by sensor type, or normal text. | . The list covers the rotation set (all groups), or the reading on the dial and the rest of its sensor group when there is no set. Colors are saved per reading and follow it through rotation, reordering and groups. Individual reading colors work whatever Accent colors is set to, and on Paper; only a valid custom text color overrides them. Switching views, or removing and adding a reading again, keeps its saved color. Labels, units, the footer, trend lines and the selection mark keep their usual styling. Production-rendered sample data, drawn with Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. Only the number colors differ between the two faces; geometry and words are the same. Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel in a simulated host with sample data, showing the Display section with individual reading colors; the full panel opens from the image. Shared Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. Color numbers by sensor type is off by default. It needs Text color on Theme text or Dimmed, and Accent colors on By sensor type under Advanced, Shared defaults. Numbers then take their sensor type’s accent color. On the Paper theme, and for readings whose type has no accent, numbers keep normal text. Theme text keeps chosen reading colors exact; Dimmed dims them. A valid Custom color for text overrides reading colors. Warning and critical values keep priority. Leave both number-color controls at their defaults to keep normal text. See Themes and colors.

127.title: Gestures
127.content: These are the Legacy preset’s gestures, which every dial runs until you pick another preset. Dial controls and presets covers Elite and Custom, the pressed turn, touch zones, pause and pin, A stats reset clears and the Sensor Control key. | Gesture | Effect | . | Turn (pressed or not) | Steps through your rotation set if you built one, otherwise through the readings of the same sensor group as the reading on the dial, wrapping at both ends. The new choice is saved. Does nothing while Ignore turns is on or the dial is pinned. | . | Push (press the dial) | Resets the session min, max and average. On Legacy this happens the moment the dial goes down. | . | Touch tap (tap the screen) | Cycles the displayed number: current, session min, session max, session average, then current again. | . | Long touch (touch and hold) | Returns to the live current value. | . Without a rotation set, a turn only walks readings from the same sensor group as your current pick (CPU, GPU, Memory, Storage, Network, Battery, Fans or System), so you can step through every fan without leaving the Fans group. To reach another group, pick a reading under On the dial now, build a rotation set that crosses groups, or use the Elite preset’s pressed turn.

128.title: Rotation set, Ignore turns, and Auto cycle
128.content: Three settings control how rotation moves. Rotation set. Tick readings in the Readings to rotate through search (in the Rotation group under Reading) to build a list. The dial then rotates through only those readings, in list order, wrapping at both ends. Ticking never changes the reading on the dial; the On the dial now picker above it does that. The set can mix readings from different sensor groups. | The ticked readings show as a list under the search, in rotation order. Select one and use Earlier, Later, Rename or Remove in the toolbar under the list. In the list, Option with Left or Right Arrow moves the selected reading, Option+Home and Option+End move it to either end, F2 renames it and Delete removes it. | The reading on the dial right now is highlighted. Turn the dial, jump groups or let the auto cycle run with the panel open, and the highlight moves with it. | A ticked reading this Mac is not reporting right now keeps its place, shows a missing pill and is skipped until it returns. The note under the list counts only the readings the dial steps through, for example Rotation moves through these 3 readings only, in this order. | Two listed readings with the same name carry a short tag that tells them apart: a word from the sensor group’s name when that differs, otherwise no. 1, no. 2 in the order the reading picker lists them. | When the reading on the dial is not in the set, a line under the list says the next step leaves it and names where it goes. | A set with one reading does not move; the note under the list says Only one reading picked. Rotation needs two or more to move. When fewer than two listed readings are reported right now, rotation waits until another returns. | Leave the set empty for the default same-group behavior. | Split into groups under the list turns the set into named rotation groups: a plain turn then stays inside one group and a pressed turn (Elite) jumps between groups. | . Ignore turns. A checkbox under Controls, shown as Ignore turns (protects against accidental bumps). The dial ignores plain and pressed turns, so a bump against the deck cannot move you off the reading you chose. This covers every command a turn carries, including Cycle stat mode on Custom. Push, touch, touch zones, the auto cycle, the settings panel and Sensor Control keys still work. Auto cycle. A select under Controls: Off (default), Every 5 seconds, Every 10 seconds, Every 30 seconds, Every minute or Every 5 minutes. It steps to the next reading in the rotation set, or in the sensor group when there is no set. | It runs even while turns are ignored. For hands-off rotation, build a set, tick Ignore turns and set a cycle time. | Any move of the selection, by hand or by the cycle, restarts the timer for a full interval. | Each step clears a custom title just like a manual turn, unless Title when the dial moves on is Stays for this dial. | Timing follows Read every: the cycle checks on each read, so a step can land up to one read late. | While the saved reading is missing, the cycle holds and tries again on the next read. It does not run while paused or pinned. | Auto cycle jumps to a critical reading (under Alerts) makes the cycle alert-aware: it holds instead of rotating away while the reading on the dial is critical, and its next step goes to a critical member of the set instead of the next one in order. A manual turn can still move away; the next step returns to a reading that is still critical. Unticked (the default), alerts do not steer the cycle. Only critical counts, not warning. See thresholds and mixed units. | . Rotation also protects your selection when the saved reading is missing (a sensor this Mac stopped reporting, or a reading not yet available after a restart): turns, the auto cycle and Sensor Control selection commands leave the dial where it is until the reading returns.

129.title: Session stats are the dial’s own, per reading
129.content: A dial calculates its own local min, max and average for each reading from the observations it receives, separate from the MIN, MAX and AVG that Sensor Reading keys and detail tiles show (how those are calculated). The average is the sum of accepted observations divided by their count; it is not time-weighted. A repeated display of the same observation does not count again; a new acquisition with the same value does. | The reading on the dial, every rotation-set member and the readings in an overview’s list collect while sensors are being read. Ordinary rotation keeps each reading’s session, so turning away and back finds it again. | A dial that goes off screen (another page or profile) keeps its pause and pin for up to 30 minutes; the plugin keeps the state of the 64 most recently hidden dials. Its sessions are kept too, and keep collecting, while a Sensor Reading key (the Back tile included), another Sensor Dial or a detail tile is visible. A visible Sensor Control key does not keep sensors being read. | A missing or non-finite reading, or a change of a reading’s unit or type, ends that reading’s session. A status screen ends every session on every dial; the first live frame afterwards shows stats reset: data gap once. The next accepted observation starts a new session. | With no Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile visible for 2 seconds (Sensor Control keys do not count), the plugin stops reading sensors. A dial that comes back after that starts its sessions again and shows stats reset: data gap once; its pause and pin stay within the limits above. A dial that comes back within those 2 seconds, as on a page change, keeps its sessions (When reading starts and stops). | Push resets the current reading under the Legacy preset. A stats reset clears can widen a reset to the rotation set or to every dial. Other presets can put the reset on another gesture. | .

130.title: How a dial’s statistics can differ from a key’s
130.content: A dial and a Sensor Reading key both count one sample per acquisition and average without time weighting. Both start over when the reading goes missing, when its unit or type changes, and when the plugin stops reading sensors. Their numbers can still differ: . | Difference | Sensor Reading key and detail tile | Sensor Dial | . | Reads counted | Every accepted read since the plugin last started reading sensors, including reads before the key appeared or picked the reading | Only reads made while this dial follows the reading (on the dial, in its rotation set or in an overview’s list), from when it first followed it | . | Reset | None | A gesture or a Sensor Control key, as far as A stats reset clears reaches | . | Status screens | The screen itself resets nothing; a reading removed or expired behind it starts over | Any status screen ends every session on every dial | . | Shared or separate | One set per reading, the same on every key and detail tile | Each dial keeps its own | .

131.title: Settings
131.content: The panel groups settings under Reading, Display, Alerts, Controls and Advanced. Its header shows the current face, the reading’s name and the data state, for example Live · Mac sensors. When something needs fixing, a status message under the header names the repair. The theme strip sits below the header. The theme strip, Reading and Display start open; the other sections start folded. A folded section summarizes its settings on its title line. Open all sections and Fold all sections in the header, or Option-click a section title (the panel’s tooltip says Alt-click), change them together. The plugin remembers which sections you left open for every Sensor Dial panel until the plugin restarts. | Section | Setting | What it does | . | Theme strip | Theme | Default follows the shared theme; a named theme (Void, Graphite, Ultraviolet, Midnight, Forest, Ember, Paper) applies to this dial only. On Default, Change opens the shared Theme under Advanced, Shared defaults. On a theme picked for this dial, Make shared makes it the shared theme and sets this dial back to Default. See Themes and colors. | . | Reading | On the dial now | A searchable picker over every reading this Mac reports, each with its value when the list loaded; the button beside it reloads the sensor list. The line under it names what else changes the reading on this dial, from the dial’s control map, for example Turns change this too. Arrow keys browse, Return picks, Tab or a click elsewhere closes without changing anything. | . | Reading | Readings to rotate through | The Rotation group: a search whose results tick readings in or out, then the ticked readings in rotation order with the Earlier, Later, Rename and Remove toolbar, and Split into groups. Empty means every reading of the picked reading’s sensor group. See Rotation set. | . | Reading | Title on the dial | A custom title. Blank uses the reading’s own name, or the name given with Rename. | . | Reading | Title when the dial moves on | Clears (default): a custom title clears whenever the dial moves on to another reading, by a turn, a press or touch set to step, a Sensor Control key or the auto cycle. Picking a reading in the settings panel keeps it. Stays for this dial keeps it as a fixed title. | . | Display | Text color | Default (follows the shared Text color and names it, for example Default (shared: Theme text)), Theme text, Dimmed or Custom color. Custom adds Custom text color and Dim labels, units and stats (the value keeps the exact color). | . | Display | View | One reading (default), Overview, two rows (big values and trend) or Overview, three rows. See Views. | . | Display | Decimals | Auto (default), or a fixed 0, 1, 2 or 3. Auto shows two decimals below 10, one below 100 and none from 100, and shortens values from 10,000 with k, M, G or T; byte and rate units follow the shared Data units setting instead. | . | Display | °F (under Temperature) | Shows temperatures in °F instead of °C. | . | Display | Row labels | Overviews only: Shorten shared words; name on the context line (default) or Always full labels. | . | Display | Context line | Three rows only: Above the rows (default) or Below the rows. | . | Display | Separators | Three rows only: Thin lines (default) or None. | . | Display | Color numbers by sensor type | Overviews only: numbers take their sensor type’s color. Off by default. See Reading colors. | . | Display | Reading colors | Overviews only: a preset or individual number colors, with Auto to reset a reading. See Reading colors. | . | Display | Bar from / Bar to | One reading only: fixed ends of the range bar. Leave blank to follow the session low and high. A decimal comma such as 30,5 works. Anything else is kept as typed, and the field says Not a number. The bar ignores this field until it is one. See Bar range. | . | Alerts | Warn at / Critical at | Values at which the bar fill, or an overview row’s value, turns amber or red. Empty means off. Use the displayed temperature unit. | . | Alerts | Alert when the value drops to or below these numbers (for fans and clocks) | Flips the comparison, for fan speeds and other readings where lower is worse. Mac Sensors offers no clock readings. | . | Alerts | Auto cycle jumps to a critical reading in the rotation and holds there while it stays critical | Makes the auto cycle alert-aware. Off by default. | . | Controls | Gestures | Legacy (default), Elite or Custom. Under it the panel lists what each gesture does on this dial now. Custom adds one select per gesture: Turn, Pressed turn, Short push, Long push, Touch tap, Long touch. See Dial controls and presets. | . | Controls | Touch zones | Elite and Custom only: Off (the whole strip is one tap) (default), Two: left and right switch readings, or Three: left and right switch, center taps. | . | Controls | Ignore turns | Disables plain and pressed turns, for bump protection. | . | Controls | Auto cycle | Steps through the rotation on a timer, every 5 seconds to every 5 minutes. Off by default. | . | Controls | A stats reset clears | This reading only (default), The whole rotation set, or Every dial, everywhere (use with care). | . | Controls | Link ID | An optional name. Sensor Control keys whose Target is this name steer this dial. | . Under Alerts, the folded title line says what is set and, once a threshold is anchored to a unit, ends with that unit, such as °C readings only. Thresholds and the manual bar range are scoped to a unit: they apply only to readings in the unit that was on the dial when you last changed any of them, so a temperature limit never fires on a fan you rotate to. Details are on Dial controls and presets. Alerts check the current value in the reading’s own unit (°F when °F is on). For bytes and rates, that is the sensor source’s number and unit, which the dial may show rescaled by Data units.

132.title: Bar range: fixed vs. session
132.content: By default (both fields blank), the bar spans the session low to high, so the fill uses the whole width of the range you have actually seen and grows as new extremes appear. Set Bar from and Bar to to fix the scale instead, for example 0 and 100 for a percentage, or 30 and 90 for a temperature, so the fill position means the same thing every time you look. You can set one end only; the other stays automatic. A range with no width yet (one observation so far) draws the fill at half. With Warn at or Critical at set, the bar’s track also marks the threshold zones in muted amber and red, toward the alarmed end (the low end when alerts fire on a drop). An automatic end widens to keep the zones visible, with a small margin past the threshold. A manual Bar from or Bar to is never widened; zones outside it are cut off. The zones show where the thresholds sit on the track and keep their muted color. The fill is the live value at full strength: the accent color normally, amber or red while alerting.

133.title: Alerts on a dial
133.content: Dials take the same Warn at and Critical at thresholds as keys, compared against the live value. A dial stays in its theme while alerting; what changes depends on the view: . | In the one-reading view, only the range bar’s fill turns amber for warning or red for critical. The title, value and the rest of the face keep your theme. | The two overview layouts have no range bar, so an alerting row’s value takes the alert color, adjusted for contrast against that row’s background. | . Alert colors take priority over individual reading colors and a custom text color. See Thresholds and alerts.

134.title: Status screens
134.content: When sensor data is not available, the touchscreen shows a short two-line message in place of a reading: . | Touchscreen | Meaning and next step | . | Reading sensors / please wait | No reading has arrived since sensor reading started, or every reading lapsed or failed before a full read had completed. Readings appear after the next successful read. | . | Source busy / retrying | The first read has not finished 15 seconds after reading started. Choose Check again in the settings panel. | . | No sensor data / copy report | Both sources answered, but no reading is current. Choose Check again; if it stays, choose Copy support report under Advanced, Support. | . | Needs macOS / check requirements | The Node runtime is not macOS on arm64 or x86_64. See Installation and requirements. | . | Bridge failed / reinstall | The native reader could not load. Quit and reopen Stream Deck. If it persists, see Keys show Bridge failed. | . | Tahoma needed / Open Font Book | A fixed image, drawn without Tahoma. Install Tahoma Bold in Font Book, then choose Check again. | . | Source error / copy report | A read failed in a way no other screen covers. Choose Check again; if it stays, choose Copy support report under Advanced, Support. | . Before you pick a reading, the dial shows Mac Sensors / rotate to pick with the hint or use the settings panel; the first turn picks a reading. If the saved reading is not reported by this Mac, the dial shows Sensor missing / waiting with the hint reselect in settings. Turns are ignored there so your saved pick survives; pick another reading in the panel if it is gone for good. The full list of status screens is on Status screens.

135.title: Advanced (shared by all keys and dials)
135.content: Shared defaults and Connection affect every Mac Sensors key and dial. | Shared defaults: Theme, Text color, the Text font: Tahoma Bold line with its status, Accent colors (By sensor type or Theme accent everywhere) and Data units (Decimal (KB, MB, GB; rates in Mbps) or Binary (KiB, MiB, GiB; rates in MiB/s)). Sensor setup lists the first steps. See Data sources. | Support: Copy support report copies a redacted diagnostics report to the clipboard; nothing is uploaded. See Troubleshooting. | Configuration documents: This dial’s settings and Shared settings as JSON, each with Copy and Replace. Replace swaps the whole document, reloads the panel and keeps fields this version does not know. Replace shared settings changes every Mac Sensors key and dial and asks for a second click. | .

137.title: Sensor Dial
137.content: The Sensor Dial action shows Mac Sensors readings on the touchscreen above a Stream Deck + or Stream Deck + XL dial. Choose one reading with a range bar, two readings with trend lines, or three compact rows. Turn the dial to change the reading; push and touch it to control the display. Requires: a Stream Deck + or + XL. Set View under Display for the layout, and Gestures under Controls for what the dial’s inputs do. Dial gestures have not yet been run on a physical Stream Deck +. The gesture map on this page and on Dial controls and presets is what the code implements and its tests check. Requirements and what has been measured are on Hardware compatibility. Production-rendered sample data with Mac catalog readings under custom labels and illustrative values, drawn with Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. The minimum, maximum and session tag are local session statistics.

138.title: Settings
138.content: The header shows the face the plugin last drew for this key, the reading’s name and group, and a data state such as Live · Mac sensors or Saved reading not found. When the data or the saved selection needs attention, a message under the header names the next step and offers buttons such as Check again, Sensor setup, Reload sensor list or Pick another reading. The theme strip, Reading and Display start open. Alerts, Press and Advanced start folded, and each folded title carries a one-line summary of what is in force, for example Warn ≥ 75 °C · critical ≥ 90 °C. The two buttons at the top right open or fold every section, and Option-click on a section title (the panel calls it Alt-click) does the same. The plugin remembers which sections you left open for each kind of panel while it runs. Folds are not saved with any key, and a restart shows the defaults again. Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel in a simulated host with sample data and Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere: Void set on this key, CPU super core 1 labeled CPU super 1, a sparkline, and sample thresholds of 75 and 90.

140.title: Reading
140.content: Type part of a reading or group name in Reading. Every word you type must appear in the group name or the reading’s label, so airflow lists Airflow left and Airflow right, and gpu 3 finds GPU 3. Results are grouped under CPU, GPU, Memory, Storage, Network, Battery, Fans and System, and each row shows its value when the list loaded and, where it has one, its type, such as Temp, Fan or Power. Reload the sensor list, the button beside the box, fetches the list again. Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel on a simulated host with sample readings and Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. It is not the Stream Deck app’s own window. Arrow keys move through the results and Return picks the highlighted one. Return with nothing typed and nothing highlighted closes the list and keeps the saved reading. Tab or a click elsewhere closes the list without changing anything. The key saves the reading’s identity, so a change in the list’s order never retargets a key. System readings (CPU usage, memory, swap, startup volume, network and storage) have fixed identities. SMC readings (temperatures, fans, power, voltage and current) include the Mac model in their identity, so a profile moved to a different model keeps its system readings and shows Sensor missing for SMC readings. Data sources explains identities. Sensor missing / pick again means this Mac does not report the saved reading right now. The key keeps the reading with its label and colors and shows it again when this Mac reports it. The panel offers Reload sensor list and Pick another reading. A reading can be absent briefly: . | CPU usage and the network and storage rates need two reads to compute. They are missing for about a quarter second when reading starts (When reading starts and stops), and for one read after the Mac sleeps. | The network or storage rates skip one read when the set of network interfaces or storage devices changes. | A failed SMC read removes that reading until a later read succeeds. | . When the whole source is unavailable, the key shows a status screen instead.

141.title: Label on the key
141.content: Custom text for the key. Leave it blank, or only spaces, to use the reading’s own name from the Mac catalog. A short label draws at the largest of three sizes, a longer one steps down, and only a label too wide for the smallest size is cut with an ellipsis. Label sizes come from measured Tahoma Bold glyph widths. A MIN, MAX or AVG badge sits in its own gap under the label, so it never takes label width. In the quad grid with small labels turned on, each label becomes a cell label of at most four characters; see the quad grid.

142.title: Theme
142.content: Pick a theme in the strip under the header: Default, Void, Graphite, Ultraviolet, Midnight, Forest, Ember or Paper. | A named theme applies to this key only. | Default follows Advanced → Shared defaults → Theme, shared by every Mac Sensors key and dial. | Change opens the shared theme setting. Make shared takes its place when this key’s theme differs from the shared one: it makes that theme the shared theme and returns this key to Default. | . The line above the chips names the theme and where it comes from, such as Default (shared: Void) or Ember (set on this key). A key with no reading draws its prompt on black and shows the theme once a reading is picked. Compare themes and colors.

143.title: Text color
143.content: How the key’s text draws, first in Display: . | Default (default): follows Advanced → Shared defaults → Text color. The option names that setting, for example Default (shared: Theme text). | Theme text: the theme’s own text colors, even when the shared setting is Dimmed or Custom color. | Dimmed: the theme’s text moved toward the background, for a dark room. Values and units keep a calculated contrast of at least 4.5:1. | Custom color: your exact color for the value. Custom text color appears with its hex code; until you pick a color, the key keeps theme text. Dim labels, units and stats (the value keeps the exact color) draws labels, units and the stat badge in the same hue closer to the background. Unticked (the default), every text element uses the exact color. | . Text color changes numbers, labels and units. Sparklines, bars, rings and their tracks keep the theme or type accent. The stat badge takes the accent with Theme text, a dimmed accent with Dimmed, and your color with Custom color. Warning and critical colors replace every text choice while a key alerts. Details: Text: Theme, Dimmed or Custom.

144.title: Value shown (stat mode)
144.content: What the number on the key shows: . | Option | Shows | . | Current value (default) | The live reading. | . | Minimum | The lowest value accepted for this reading since the plugin last started reading sensors, with a MIN badge. | . | Maximum | The highest value accepted since then, with a MAX badge. | . | Average | The arithmetic mean of the values accepted since then, with an AVG badge. | . Production-rendered sample data with sample session statistics, drawn with Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. macOS reports current values only, so Mac Sensors keeps these statistics itself, for every reading this Mac reports. Changing pages, opening sensor details and pressing Back keep the statistics, because reading continues for 2 seconds after the last Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile disappears (When reading starts and stops). Each accepted read adds one sample, including a read that repeats the last value, so the average counts reads and is not weighted by time. On the first read after the plugin starts reading sensors, MIN, MAX and AVG all equal the current value. The statistics follow Decimals, °F and Data units the same way the live value does. Statistics are kept per reading. Every Sensor Reading key and detail tile that shows the same reading shows the same MIN, MAX and AVG. A key you add, or switch to another reading, shows that reading’s statistics at once, including reads made before the change. A reading’s statistics start over: . | after a gap in that reading: a read where it is missing or withheld (invalid, out of range or duplicated), or a failed read of its source, which removes every reading from that source; | when the reading expires, 15 seconds after its last accepted read, for example across a sleep longer than that; | when the reading’s unit or type changes; | for CPU usage and the network and storage rates, after any sleep, because they skip one read; the rates also skip one when the set of network interfaces or storage devices changes; | when the plugin stops reading sensors, 2 seconds after the last Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile disappears, which ends every reading’s statistics. They are kept in memory only, so a plugin restart also starts them over. | . Changing Read every keeps them; it clears sparklines only. There is no reset for a key’s statistics. With the default A press, the How Display works fold says: Pressing the key cycles current, min, max and avg. Min, max and avg come from this session’s reads; they start over after a gap in the reading, or when no Mac Sensors key, dial or detail tile has been shown for 2 seconds. Sensor Control keys do not count as shown. A Sensor Dial keeps separate statistics of its own, which can differ from a key’s for the same reading; see Session stats are the dial’s own, per reading. Alert colors and Bar and Ring fills follow the live value whatever Value shown says. A key showing MAX keeps its normal colors while the live value is back under Warn at, even when the maximum is past it.

145.title: Layout: two readings on one key
145.content: Choose Readings on this key → Two readings, stacked, then pick Reading 2 and an optional Label 2. Until Reading 2 is picked, the key keeps one reading and the panel says This layout draws once another reading is picked below. Until then the key shows one reading. Row 2 shows sets the second row’s statistic: . | The same stat as row 1 (default): a press cycles both rows together, with one badge in the divider. | Always the current value, Always the minimum, Always the maximum or Always the average: row 2 stays put while a press cycles row 1. Each row that shows a statistic gets its own badge on its label line; matching statistics share the divider badge. | . Each row shows its own reading’s statistics. For a minimum and maximum pair, set Value shown to Minimum and Row 2 shows to Always the maximum. Useful pairs are CPU super core 1 above GPU 1, or Network receive above Network send. Rules for every multi-reading layout: . | Warn at and Critical at watch the first reading only and recolor the whole key. Put the reading you need alerts on first, or give it its own key. The Alerts help then adds Only reading 1 is checked; it recolors the whole key. and the folded summary ends in first reading. | Decimals and °F apply to every reading. The type accent follows the first reading. | Graph under the value is for one reading only. It stays saved while hidden. | A reading this Mac does not report shows a dash while the others continue. In two and three rows its row keeps its custom label, or reads Sensor missing. If every picked reading is missing, the key shows Sensor missing / pick again. | Changing layouts keeps readings, labels and colors. Reading 2 serves all three multi-reading layouts, and Reading 3 serves both three rows and the quad grid. Switching to One reading draws the single face again. | .

146.title: Layout: three readings in rows
146.content: Choose Readings on this key → Three readings, rows, then set Reading 2 and Reading 3, with optional Label 2 and Label 3. Each row has a left-aligned label and a right-aligned value with its unit. The layout needs the first reading and at least one more; an unpicked row stays empty. All rows show the same statistic and a press cycles them together; the badge appears once, on the first separator. Values share one size, and a long label shortens so its number stays whole. The panel says so: A long name shortens so its number stays whole. Every row shows the same stat. The multi-reading rules apply, and this layout has no graph strip.

147.title: Layout: four readings in a quad grid
147.content: Choose Readings on this key → Four readings, quad grid. The first reading is top left, Reading 2 top right, Reading 3 bottom left and Reading 4 bottom right. It needs the first reading and at least one more; unpicked cells stay empty. Cell colors in Display tells the cells apart: . | Signal (four hues) (default): blue #4CC2FF, rose #FF7E8E, green #38CD89 and gold #D4AB33. | Pairs (top row, bottom row): blue on top, rose below. | Uniform (accent blue): blue in every cell. | The four color wells set one cell each. The preset reads Custom when the four colors match no preset. | . Show a small label in each cell (values then use the text color) puts a short label in the cell color above each value, and values take the key’s Text color. With Custom color, the labels take the custom color’s secondary shade instead of the cell color. Unticked (default), values take the cell colors. With small labels on, cell labels come from Label on the key and Label 2, Label 3 and Label 4, or else from the first word of the reading’s name. They are upper-cased and cut at four characters, and the label fields say 4 chars max in this layout. Startup volume available becomes STAR, so give it a label such as FREE. Values compact to four characters at most: decimals drop first, then large numbers shorten, such as 48700 to 49k. A press cycles every cell through the same statistic, with one badge at the center. The multi-reading rules apply, and the layout has no graph strip. The automatic cell colors are lifted for contrast against the background when needed. Colors you pick draw exactly with Theme text and are only blended toward the background with Dimmed; they are never lifted for contrast, so check them on your deck. A Custom color text setting replaces the cell colors, and so does a warning or critical alert. Themes and colors explains color precedence.

148.title: Decimals
148.content: . | Auto (default): precision follows the size of the number. Below 10 shows two decimals, from 10 one, from 100 none, and from 10,000 a k, M, G or T suffix (48700 reads 48.7k). | 0, 1, 2 or 3: that many decimal places. | . Byte quantities and transfer rates rescale through their own units instead; see Data units. Auto shows zero as 0.00, so a stopped fan reads 0.00 RPM. Choose 0 for fan keys.

149.title: Temperature unit
149.content: The °F box under Temperature converts °C readings to Fahrenheit for display. Every Mac temperature arrives in °C; other units are unchanged. Thresholds compare against the displayed unit, so a key switched to °F needs its thresholds in °F (80 °C is 176 °F). A sparkline keeps its line through the switch.

150.title: Graph under the value: sparkline, bar, ring
150.content: Graph under the value in Display adds one strip under the value. It shows only on the one-reading layout: . | None (default): the value alone. | Sparkline (recent history): a line of the reading’s recent samples along the bottom of the key, in the accent color over a filled track, ending in a dot at the newest sample. | Bar (value in its range): a horizontal gauge showing where the live value sits in its range. | Ring (value in its range): the same gauge as an arc around the value, opening downward. | . Bar and Ring find their range automatically, and there are no bounds to type: . | Percentages run 0 to 100. On Mac that is CPU usage. | Every other reading spans the values seen: the reading’s MIN and MAX since the plugin last started reading sensors (see Value shown), the live value, and the recent samples the plugin holds for it, up to 36. The range therefore keeps its width when a Read every change clears the samples. While MIN and MAX are still equal, the range has no width, and the fill sits at the halfway point unless a threshold widens it. | Warn at and Critical at draw amber and red zones toward the alarmed end: the high end normally, the low end when the direction box is ticked. The range widens to keep a zone visible, with a small margin when a threshold sits at or past the edge. | . The panel’s range sentence also mentions Yes/No readings, which run 0 to 1; the current Mac catalog has none. Zones draw as muted shades: the alert color blended 45 percent toward the key background. They mark positions; the fill on top shows the live value in the accent color. While the key alerts, the whole key takes the alert palette, and the fill and zones follow it. The fill follows the live value even while the text shows MIN, MAX or AVG. Sparkline notes: . | It holds the last 36 samples, one for each new measurement of the reading. At Read every 1 second that covers about the last 36 seconds. | The line scales to its own lowest and highest sample, so its shape shows how the reading changed recently. Identical samples draw a level line across the middle. Two samples are needed before a line draws. | Samples keep collecting for a reading a key has shown while any Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile is visible, so a key on another page resumes its line when you return. | When no reading key, dial or detail tile has been visible for 2 seconds, reading stops and every sparkline is cleared. A page change, opening sensor details or pressing Back inside those 2 seconds keeps every line. | A missing or failed reading, a change in the reading’s type or unit, a status screen, a Read every change and a plugin restart clear the history. | Switching between °C and °F keeps the line unchanged. | .

151.title: Warn at and Critical at
151.content: In Alerts. When the live value reaches Warn at, the whole key turns amber with dark text; at Critical at, red with white text. The two alert palettes are the same on every theme. Leave a field blank to turn it off; an empty field shows Off. Thresholds use the displayed temperature unit. Byte and rate thresholds use the reading’s own unit, bytes or bytes per second, before Data units rescales it. A comma works as a decimal point (70,5 is 70.5). Text that is not a number is kept as typed, ignored, and flagged under the field: Not a number. Alerts ignore this field until it is one. The folded Alerts title reads back the comparison in force, for example Warn ≥ 80 °C · critical ≥ 90 °C. It ends in first reading on a multi-reading key, and in warning now or critical now while the key alerts. See Thresholds and alerts for the full behavior and worked examples with Mac readings.

152.title: Direction
152.content: Alert when the value drops to or below these numbers (for fans and clocks) makes lower worse: the alert fires at or below each number. Use it for fan speed or free space on the startup volume. Unticked (default), higher is worse, for temperatures, power and CPU usage.

153.title: Pressing the key
153.content: By default a press cycles Value shown: current, MIN, MAX, AVG, then current again. The badge under the label follows, and the choice is saved to the key, the same as changing Value shown. MIN, MAX and AVG are the reading’s statistics since the plugin last started reading sensors, as Value shown describes; a press changes only which one the key shows and resets nothing. With the default press, a key with no reading ignores it. Alert colors keep following the live value throughout. On a two-reading key with Row 2 shows at its default, a press cycles both rows together. A row pinned to a fixed statistic stays put while the first row cycles. On the three-row and quad layouts a press cycles every reading together.

154.title: A press can open details
154.content: . Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel on a simulated host with sample readings and Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. It is not the Stream Deck app’s own window. Press → A press sets what a press does: . | Cycles current, min, max, avg (default): the cycle above. | Opens sensor details: on key down, the deck switches to a bundled detail view listing every reading in this reading’s group, a custom list, or the readings matching a filter. | Tap cycles; hold opens details: a press released within half a second cycles the statistic; holding for half a second opens details once. | . The first time details open on each kind of deck, Stream Deck asks to install the bundled detail view, and again after an update that changes it. On a deck with no fitting detail view, the panel says Sensor details are not available on this deck and a press shows the Stream Deck alert triangle instead. Sensor details covers what the view shows, its settings and which decks it supports. The detail view’s Back tile is this same Sensor Reading action with its press fixed to returning to the previous profile. Its panel says so under the header, and its Press section holds that note in place of the press choices. Everything else on this page, from the reading and layouts to the theme and thresholds, applies to it. See Configuring the Back tile.

155.title: Status screens
155.content: A two-line status replaces the value when the key cannot show a reading. The saved reading and settings stay unchanged, and the screen clears on the first read that produces a current reading. Production-rendered status screens with sample scenarios. Status screens use fixed colors, so the theme does not change them. | Key shows | Meaning | What to do | . | Pick a sensor / in settings | The key works, but no reading is selected yet. | Type in the Reading box and choose a reading. | . | Reading sensors / please wait | No reading has arrived since reading started: the first read is still out. | Wait for the first read. | . | Sensor missing / pick again | A reading is selected, but this Mac does not report it right now. | Choose Reload sensor list or Pick another reading; see Reading. | . | Source busy / retrying | 15 seconds after reading started, the first read has still not finished. | Choose Check again. | . | No sensor data / copy report | Both sources answered, but no reading is current. | Choose Check again. If it stays, choose Copy support report under Advanced → Support. | . | Needs macOS / check requirements | The plugin is not running on macOS with an arm64 or x86_64 Node runtime. | See Installation and requirements. | . 156.title: Advanced (shared by keys and dials)
156.content: Advanced holds four groups. Shared defaults and Connection are marked All keys and dials: they change every Mac Sensors key and dial on every Stream Deck. The folded title summarizes them, for example Mac sensors · read every 1 s · decimal data units. | Shared defaults: Theme, Text color (with Shared custom text color and Dim labels, units and stats), Text font, Accent colors and Data units. They apply to every key and dial left on Default; a key or dial with its own choice keeps it. See Themes and colors. | Connection: Read every sets how often the plugin reads the sensors on this Mac: 250 ms, 500 ms, 1 second (default), 2 seconds or 5 seconds. Every reading key and dial updates from that one shared read. Changing it clears sparkline history, and shorter intervals read the sensors more often and use more processor time. Data sources explains reads and timing. Sensor setup folds out three first-setup steps. | Support: Copy support report copies a redacted diagnostics report to the clipboard. Nothing is uploaded. See Troubleshooting. | Configuration documents: copy or replace this key’s settings and the shared settings. | .

157.title: Configuration documents
157.content: Two JSON wells: This key’s settings, the exact settings this key runs on, and Shared settings, marked All keys and dials. Copy fills an untouched well with the settings of that moment and puts the document on the clipboard; save it to a file to back a layout up. Paste a saved document and press Replace this key’s settings to restore it or clone it onto another key. Replacing writes the whole document at once and reloads the panel, and fields this version does not know are kept. Text that is not one JSON object is refused and nothing changes. Replace shared settings changes every Mac Sensors key and dial, so its first press only arms it: the button reads Press again to replace for all keys and dials, and a second press replaces. A double click only arms it, and leaving the button or editing the document disarms it. In the key’s document each reading identity carries the reading’s name after it, so the file stays readable; an identity with no name is a reading this Mac does not report now. Replacing strips the names, and settings always store the bare identity. The wells exist on the Sensor Reading and Sensor Dial panels only.

158.title: Data units
158.content: Data units sets how byte quantities and transfer rates read on every key and dial: . | Decimal (KB, MB, GB; rates in Mbps) (default): bytes in B, KB, MB, GB and TB (steps of 1000), and rates in bits per second, bps through Tbps (byte rates times 8). | Binary (KiB, MiB, GiB; rates in MiB/s): bytes in B, KiB, MiB, GiB and TiB (steps of 1024), and rates in bytes per second, B/s through TiB/s. | . Every Mac rate is a byte rate, including Storage read and Storage write, so under Decimal those read in Mbps too. | Reading in a live read on the measured M5 Pro | Source value | Decimal | Binary | . | Startup volume available | 292596883456 B | 293 GB | 273 GiB | . | Memory total | 68719476736 B | 68.7 GB | 64.0 GiB | . | Network send | 2909517.6 B/s | 23.3 Mbps | 2.77 MiB/s | . 165.title: Recovery
165.content: A status screen does not require removing the key. While a Sensor Reading key (including the Back tile), Sensor Dial or detail tile is visible, the plugin keeps reading at the Read every interval: . | Every read asks both sources again. A source that failed is asked again on the next read, and the other source keeps serving meanwhile. One exception: SMC readings wait for the first successful system counter read, which carries the font check. Until then keys show Source error, or Source busy if a read is still out after 15 seconds. | If the SMC connection breaks, the next read opens it again. | The font check runs on every system counter read, so Tahoma needed clears on the first read after Tahoma Bold is available. Check again is not required; it only makes that read happen at once. | A read that starts while a status screen shows never waits more than 100 ms for a slow source, so readings return at most 100 ms after their own source answers. | A page you return to after no Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile was visible anywhere for 2 seconds starts reading again and shows Reading sensors until its first read completes. A page change, opening sensor details or pressing Back inside those 2 seconds shows readings at once (When reading starts and stops). | . Bridge failed and Needs macOS do not recover by themselves; the result is kept for the life of the plugin process. For Bridge failed, quit and reopen Stream Deck. Needs macOS means the Node runtime is not a supported macOS one, which a restart does not change; see Installation and requirements. A load failure alone does not establish whether a file is damaged, missing or blocked.

167.title: Status screens
167.content: When a key or dial cannot show a current reading, it shows a two-line status screen instead. The first line names the condition; the second names the next step. In the settings panel explains what the panel shows at the same time, and Troubleshooting has the full repair path. A status screen never changes saved settings. The selected reading, its label, colors and every other setting stay as they were. Pick a sensor clears when you pick a reading, and Sensor missing when this Mac reports the saved reading again or you pick another. Bridge failed and Needs macOS last until the plugin restarts. Every other screen clears by itself on the first read that produces a current reading. Production-rendered status screens with sample scenarios. Status screens use fixed colors, so the theme does not change them.

169.title: Contrast

170.title: Shared and per-key themes
170.content: Set the shared theme in Advanced → Shared defaults → Theme. It applies to every Mac Sensors key and dial set to Default, on every Stream Deck. The panel says so: Used by every Mac Sensors key and dial, on every Stream Deck, that is set to Default. A key or dial with its own choice keeps it. A named preset stays local. One dial can keep Ember while the rest follow Midnight. On a key, the strip and Text color are described in Sensor Reading; on a dial, in Sensor Dial. A new install starts with Void as the shared theme. If no shared theme was ever saved and the plugin finds existing settings at its first start, such as a profile with configured keys imported into a new install, the shared theme starts as Graphite instead. Pick any theme to replace it.

171.title: Precedence
171.content: A key’s or dial’s own theme wins over the shared theme. Choose Default to make it follow again. A stored theme name this version does not know, for example from a configuration document made by a newer version, draws Void and stays stored. The theme line shows it as unknown, such as “neon” (unknown; draws Void), and the help under the strip says This version does not know that theme; the key keeps it stored until you pick one.

172.title: The Default chip
172.content: Default follows the shared choice. Its chip shows the shared theme’s colors with a dashed frame and a link mark, which set it apart from the preset it currently uses. The theme line says where the colors come from, such as Default (shared: Void) or Ember (set on this key). | Change opens the shared Theme setting. | Make shared appears when this key’s or dial’s theme differs from the shared one. It makes that theme the shared theme first, then returns the key or dial to Default, so its look does not change. The theme line then reads Default (shared: Ember), and a screen reader hears, for example, Ember is now the shared theme, was Void. This key follows it. If you pick another theme for the key while the shared settings save, the key keeps that newer choice. | . Folding the strip keeps the chosen chip and its source on screen. A key with no reading shows the theme once a reading is picked; until then the strip’s help says Shows on the key once a reading is picked. Void is set on this key while the shared theme is also Void, so Make shared is hidden.
