179.title: Themes and colors
179.content: Pick a theme in the strip under a key’s or dial’s settings header. Choose Default to follow the shared theme, or a named preset for that key or dial only.

180.title: The two fields
180.content: | Field | Effect on a key | Effect on a dial | . | Warn at | The whole face turns amber with near-black text | The single view’s bar fill turns amber; in an overview view, the alerting row’s value | . | Critical at | The whole face turns red with white text | The single view’s bar fill turns red; in an overview view, the alerting row’s value | . | Alert when the value drops to or below these numbers (for fans and clocks) | Makes a low value the alarm | Same | . An empty field shows Off. On a dial the fields say what will change, such as Off (bar turns amber) in the single view and Off (row value turns amber) in an overview view. Thresholds also mark the range on any face that draws one. A key whose Graph under the value is Bar or Ring, a one-reading setting, shows a muted amber zone from Warn at and a muted red zone from Critical at, running toward the alarmed end: the low end when the direction box is ticked. A dial’s range bar marks them the same way. Zones are the alert colors blended toward the face background, and the live fill draws over them. A key’s range is always automatic and widens to keep a zone visible. A dial with Bar from or Bar to set keeps those bounds, and a zone outside them is cut off. See Graph under the value.

182.title: Thresholds are in the displayed unit
182.content: The value compared is the live reading in the unit the key shows, after the °C to °F conversion. Tick °F and a Warn at of 80 fires at 80 °F, which is about 26.7 °C; every temperature in a live read on the measured M5 Pro was above that. Enter Fahrenheit numbers instead: 176 for 80 °C. Leave °F off and the same reading compares in °C. One exception: Data units rescales bytes and transfer rates for display only. Thresholds compare against the number in the reading’s own unit, bytes or bytes per second. A Startup volume available reading of 292596883456 B shows 293 GB under Decimal and compares as 292596883456. Switching Decimal and Binary never changes an alert. See Data units. | Mac readings | Unit a threshold compares in | . | Temperatures (CPU and GPU cores, Battery, NAND, Airport, Airflow) | °C, or °F with °F ticked | . | Fans | RPM | . | Power (System Total, DC In, Battery) | W | . | Voltage | V | . | Current | A | . | CPU usage | % | . | Memory total, free, active, inactive, wired and compressed; Swap used; Startup volume total and available | B (bytes) | . | Network receive and send; Storage read and write | B/s (bytes per second), also when the key shows Mbps | . Note: A key showing a MAX above Critical at draws on the normal face once the live value is back under Warn at.

183.title: The trigger is at or past the limit
183.content: Reaching the number is enough: . | Normal direction (higher is worse): alerts when the value is at or above the threshold. | Below direction (lower is worse): alerts when the value is at or below the threshold. | . Critical is checked before warning, so a reading past both limits shows critical. A value that is not a finite number never alerts.

184.title: Decimal commas are accepted
184.content: Both fields accept a period or a comma as the decimal point, so 70.5 and 70,5 both mean seventy and a half. Only the first comma counts, so do not group digits: 50,000 means 50, and a value with two commas is not a number. Blank means no threshold. Anything that is not a number is kept as typed but ignored, and the field says so under it: Not a number. Alerts ignore this field until it is one. The folded Alerts title then names the field, such as warn value is not a number, or reads Off: the values entered are not numbers when neither field is a number. The fields also accept exponent notation: 50e9 means 50000000000. That helps with byte thresholds.

185.title: Direction: alert when high or when low
185.content: By default higher is worse: the right setting for temperatures, power, CPU usage and transfer rates. Tick Alert when the value drops to or below these numbers (for fans and clocks) for readings where low is the problem: . | Fan speed, on a fan that should keep spinning. | Startup volume available, to know when free space drops under a floor. | . With the box ticked, Warn at and Critical at become floors: the alert fires when the reading falls to or below them.

186.title: Alert colors
186.content: Key alert palettes are the same on every theme: amber #E8940D with near-black text #1C1200 for warning, red #CB2114 with white text for critical. The value text calculates to about 7.6:1 on the amber and about 5.6:1 on the red. Type accents, quad cell colors and a Custom color text setting do not override them. A dial keeps its theme while alerting. Its single view fills the bar with #E8940D or #CB2114. Its overview views color the alerting row’s value #E8940D for warning and #FF3B30 for critical, adjusted toward 4.5:1 against the row background when needed. Contrast is a calculation. Physical recognition across devices and color-vision differences has not been established; for device checks, see Hardware compatibility. Themes and colors lists every alert token.

187.title: Worked examples
187.content: The readings below come from a live read on the measured M5 Pro at 15.7 percent CPU usage. The limits are example values: choose limits for your Mac and how you use it. The plugin does not offer a hardware safety limit.

188.title: CPU temperature: warn 80, critical 90
188.content: In that read, CPU super core 1 was 49.6 °C. | Warn at 80 | Critical at 90 | Alert when the value drops: unticked (higher is worse) | . Below 80 °C the key stays themed. At 80 °C it turns amber; at 90 °C, red. The folded Alerts title reads Warn ≥ 80 °C · critical ≥ 90 °C. To read the face in Fahrenheit, tick °F in Display and enter 176 and 194; the title then reads Warn ≥ 176 °F · critical ≥ 194 °F.

189.title: Fan speed: alert when it drops
189.content: A floor for a fan you expect to spin: . | Warn at 500 | Critical at 300 | Alert when the value drops: ticked | . Above 500 RPM the key is normal. At 500 or below it warns; at 300 or below it turns red, and a fan reading 0 RPM is red. In the same read, Fan 1 and Fan 2 both read 0 RPM. A floor on those fans turns the key red whenever they read 0, so use a floor only on a fan that should always spin. To catch a fan speeding up instead, leave the box unticked and set Warn at to a speed you choose. Set Decimals to 0 on fan keys: Auto shows 0 RPM as 0.00.

190.title: Free space on the startup volume
190.content: Startup volume available reports bytes. In the same read it was 292596883456 B, which the key shows as 293 GB under Decimal or 273 GiB under Binary. Enter the limits in bytes: . | Warn at 50000000000 or 50e9 (50 GB) | Critical at 20000000000 or 20e9 (20 GB) | Alert when the value drops: ticked | . When free space drops to 50 GB the key turns amber, and at 20 GB red. The folded title reads Warn ≤ 50000000000 B · critical ≤ 20000000000 B. If you think in binary units, 50 GiB is 53687091200.

191.title: Network rate in bits
191.content: Network receive reports bytes per second, and Decimal shows bits per second. To warn at 100 Mbps, enter 12500000: 100 million bits per second divided by 8. In the same read, Network send was 2909517.6 B/s, shown as 23.3 Mbps. Tip: With the below direction, set Critical at lower than Warn at: critical is the deeper floor. Because critical is checked first, an inverted pair (Warn at 300, Critical at 500, box ticked) turns red at 500 and never shows amber. The same holds in the normal direction: a Critical at below Warn at turns red first.

192.title: Where thresholds live
192.content: Warn at, Critical at and the direction box are in the Alerts section of both the Sensor Reading and Sensor Dial settings panels, below Display. The folded title states the rule in force and whether it is firing now (warning now, critical now). There is one pair of limits per key and per dial, saved with the rest of that action’s settings (Sensor Reading settings, Sensor Dial settings). On the Two readings, stacked, Three readings, rows and Four readings, quad grid key layouts, that one pair watches the first reading only. The other rows or cells never raise an alert of their own, and the whole key recolors when the first reading crosses. The Alerts help says Only reading 1 is checked; it recolors the whole key. Put the reading you want alerts on first, or give it its own key. On a dial, thresholds and the manual bar range apply only to readings in the unit that was on the dial when you last changed any of them, because rotation can put readings with different units on one dial: a °C limit never fires on a fan you rotate to. The folded title adds the unit, such as °C readings only. A dial can also jump to a critical reading with Auto cycle jumps to a critical reading in the rotation and holds there while it stays critical. Details: Alerts on a dial and Thresholds and mixed units. In a detail view, reading tiles draw without alert colors. A Back tile with its own reading follows its own Alerts settings; an unconfigured Back tile shows the opener’s reading with the opener’s thresholds.

193.title: Where to go next
193.content: . | Sensor Reading: where the fields sit on a key, with Bar and Ring zones. | Alerts on a dial: bar fill, overview rows and unit scoping. | Themes and colors: the alert palettes against every theme. | Troubleshooting: when an alert does not fire. | .

194.title: Thresholds and alerts
194.content: Set Warn at, Critical at or both to change the display when the live value reaches a limit: amber for warning, red for critical. Open Alerts in the key or dial settings. Thresholds use the current value, even while a key shows MIN, MAX or AVG. Both fields are optional and independent. A key with neither set shows its themed value. Alerts change only what the plugin shows: colors, and with Auto cycle jumps to a critical reading ticked, which reading a dial shows. They never write to the Mac. The SMC transport accepts read and key-information requests only, so an alert cannot change a fan speed or a power limit. Production-rendered sample data: Mac catalog readings with the custom label CPU super 1 on the first three faces, and illustrative values. Warn at 60 and Critical at 80 for the amber face, Warn at 40 and Critical at 60 for the red face, both with a bar, and Warn at 65 and Critical at 85 for the CPU usage bar. Rendered with Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere, so the normal faces use the Void accent instead of the default type accents.

195.title: How to read a status screen
195.content: When a key cannot show a current reading, it shows a two-line status screen. Dials use the same words in their title and value lines. The screen names the condition the plugin established; it may not identify the underlying cause. Saved settings never change because of a status screen. Production-rendered status screens with sample scenarios. Status screens use fixed colors, so the theme does not change them. | Key shows | Dial shows | Meaning | . | Reading sensors / please wait | Reading sensors / please wait | The first read since reading started has not returned yet. | . | Source busy / retrying | Source busy / retrying | The first read has not finished after 15 seconds. | . | No sensor data / copy report | No sensor data / copy report | Both sources answered, but no reading is current. | . | Tahoma needed / Open Font Book | Tahoma needed / Open Font Book | Tahoma Bold was not found. Fixed image. | . | Bridge failed / reinstall | Bridge failed / reinstall | The native reader could not be used. | . | Source error / copy report | Source error / copy report | A read failed with no more specific cause. | . | Needs macOS / check requirements | Needs macOS / check requirements | The Node runtime that started the plugin is not macOS on arm64 or x86_64. | . | Pick a sensor / in settings | Mac Sensors / rotate to pick | No reading selected yet. | . | Sensor missing / pick again | Sensor missing / waiting | The selected reading is not reported right now. | . Status screens has the panel sentence and buttons for each screen.

196.title: Keys show Reading sensors
196.content: The first read after reading started has not returned yet. It clears when that read returns, with no action from you. Reading starts again when a page comes back after no Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile was visible for 2 seconds, so that page starts here too; a page change, opening details or Back inside those 2 seconds does not (When reading starts and stops). It can also return during use if every reading lapses or fails before the session’s first SMC read has answered. If it stays for more than 15 seconds: . | Choose Check again in the key’s settings. | If it still stays, copy a support report first, then quit and reopen the Stream Deck app, which restarts the plugin. | If it comes back, file an issue with the report and the plugin log. | .

197.title: Keys show Source busy
197.content: 15 seconds after reading started, the first read has still not finished: no system counter read has succeeded and at least one source has not answered. The plugin has not checked the font yet. | Choose Check again. Each read asks the sources again; a source whose earlier call is still running is asked again once that call returns. | If it stays, copy a support report before anything else: it describes the running plugin, and a restart replaces it. Its dataSource section shows the reason, and its mac section shows how many readings each source returned (sourceRows) and any source error (sourceErrors). Until a source has been accepted the mac section says catalog: "not sampled", and a read that failed without answering leaves no sourceErrors entry; the plugin log then has a read failed; retrying. line. | Then quit and reopen the Stream Deck app. A hardware call that is already running cannot be cancelled. Quitting and reopening the app starts a new plugin process; whether that clears a stuck call has not been tested. | .

198.title: Keys show No sensor data
198.content: Both sources have answered, but no reading is current: every reading failed, was withheld as invalid, or expired. | The Mac just woke from sleep. After a sleep longer than 15 seconds every reading has expired, and this screen can show until the first read after waking returns. Wait for the next read. Real sleep and wake on hardware has not been checked yet; see Sleep and wake. | Both sources are failing. Choose Check again. Look in the plugin log for smc readings unavailable; other sources continue., public readings unavailable; other sources continue. or read failed; retrying. lines. | Copy a support report and file an issue with the log lines. | .

199.title: Keys show Tahoma needed
199.content: On every system counter read, the native reader asks macOS for the font with the exact PostScript name Tahoma-Bold, with automatic font activation turned off. Any other answer, such as a substitute font, counts as missing. Readings are hidden while it is missing, because their text is fitted to Tahoma Bold. The Tahoma needed screen is stored as pixels, so it draws without the font, and the Back tile keeps its return arrow. Tahoma Bold ships with macOS; on the measured macOS 27.0.1 it is in /System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental. | Open Font Book and search for Tahoma. | Make sure Tahoma Bold is installed and turned on. Install it if it is not listed. | Wait for the next read, at most one Read every interval while a Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile is visible, or choose Check again in the key’s settings to read at once. | . Check again is not required. The font check runs with every system counter read, so the screen clears on the first read after Tahoma Bold is available; Check again only makes that read happen now. The panel sentence still says “Install Tahoma Bold in Font Book, then choose Check again.” Recovery after a real font install has been tested only with simulated reads; no system font was removed from the measured Mac. Your readings, labels, colors and other settings stay as they were, and the same readings return. The panel header says No sensor data while this screen shows; the message under it gives the font instruction. Do not remove or replace system fonts to test this.

200.title: Keys show Bridge failed
200.content: Before loading its native reader, the plugin checks it. When the Stream Deck app’s Node runtime runs as arm64 it uses bin/hwmac-arm64.node, and as x86_64 it uses bin/hwmac-x86_64.node. The file’s SHA-256 must match bin/native-artifacts.json, and its build information (protocol, version, source identity, Node-API level, architecture, macOS, not a test build) must match this plugin. Bridge failed means a check failed or macOS would not load the file. A load failure alone does not establish whether the file is damaged, missing or blocked. The result is kept for the life of the plugin process. | Quit and reopen Stream Deck. The new plugin process checks the reader again. | If it persists, export a backup of your Stream Deck profiles, remove Mac Sensors as described in Removing, then open the .streamDeckPlugin package again. Removing and reinstalling the same version has not been run on the measured Mac yet. | If the screen returns, copy a support report and file an issue. Include the package’s SHA-256 from shasum -a 256 and the release you got it from. | . See also Opening the same version again does nothing. Do not copy files over the installed plugin folder while the plugin is running. The native files are ad-hoc signed. codesign --verify --strict checks a file’s integrity; it is not a Developer ID or notarization check.

201.title: Keys show Source error
201.content: A read failed in a way no other screen covers. Known causes: the native reader’s clock returned no usable time, or both sources answered but the system counter read failed, so the font check that runs with it could not run. Every cause shows the same panel sentence. | Choose Check again. | If it stays, copy a support report first and keep the plugin log. The report gives the reason; the log can carry the source warnings listed under Reading the plugin log. | Then quit and reopen the Stream Deck app. | .

202.title: Keys show Needs macOS
202.content: The Node runtime that started the plugin is not macOS on arm64 or x86_64, so the plugin does not load its reader. With the runtime the Stream Deck app supplies, this screen is not expected; the package declares macOS only. Check Installation and requirements, then copy a support report: its mac section shows the platform and processor architecture the runtime reported.

203.title: Keys show Sensor missing
203.content: A reading is selected, but this Mac does not report it right now. The saved identity no longer resolves in the latest read. The plugin never moves the key to a reading with a similar name or list position. Causes, most lasting first: . | This Mac does not have that reading. An SMC reading’s identity includes the Mac model, so a selection saved on another model, or copied in a configuration document from another Mac, is missing here. An SMC key that this model does not have is never reported. See Data sources. | Its last read failed or was withheld. When the SMC read fails, the SMC readings drop out while the system counters keep working. When a system counter read fails after an earlier one succeeded, the system readings drop out and the SMC readings keep working. If no system counter read has succeeded since reading started, keys show Source error, or Source busy while a read is still out after 15 seconds, because the font has not been checked yet. A value outside its accepted range is withheld. | It is a worked-out reading waiting for its pair. CPU usage and the transfer rates show this for about a quarter second after reading starts, for one read after a sleep, and network rates for one read when an interface counter starts over at 4 GiB. See Counter rebaseline. | . The settings panel tells this apart from a source problem. Its header says Saved reading not found, and the message under it says the key keeps the saved reading with its label and colors and shows it again when this Mac reports it, with Reload sensor list and Pick another reading buttons. Fix: for a temporary cause, wait; the reading returns by itself under the same identity. If the reading is gone for good, choose Pick another reading and select one from the list on this Mac. A dial shows Sensor missing / waiting and ignores turns while the reading is gone, so a dropout cannot move it off your saved pick.

204.title: Keys show Access denied or Not updating
204.content: These two screens are defined, but no read in version 1.0.1 reports them. When the SMC service cannot be opened, the SMC readings are left out and the system counters keep working; a reading older than 15 seconds is removed rather than held. If you see either screen, copy a support report, keep the plugin log and file an issue.

205.title: The panel says the plugin is not responding
205.content: The header reads The plugin is not responding when no answer comes within 3 seconds of the panel opening. The message under it says “The Mac Sensors plugin is not answering this panel. Settings you change here are still saved; restarting the Stream Deck app restarts the plugin.” Copy support report changes to Plugin not responding when no report arrives within 3 seconds. Keys and dials can stop changing without any status screen. This combination says the plugin is not answering the app. It does not identify why. | Quit and reopen the Stream Deck app. | Make sure the installed version is the current release. | If it happens again, keep the plugin log from before the restart (the older numbered file) and file an issue. | .

206.title: The picker is empty
206.content: The Reading list shows the readings of the latest read, grouped by CPU, GPU, Memory, Storage, Network, Battery, Fans and System. Settings-panel capture of the staged 1.0.1.0 panel on a simulated host with sample readings and Accent colors set to Theme accent everywhere. It is not the Stream Deck app’s own window. | A status screen is showing. The message under the panel header names the cause, with Check again and Sensor setup. Fix that first. | The search is too narrow. The list then says No readings match "…" with your text. Clear the search box. | The list has not loaded. The reload button beside the search box (“Reload the sensor list”) reloads the list from the latest read. Check again asks for a new read. | The reading is not offered on any Mac. CPU and GPU clocks, GPU usage, per-chip power and HID temperatures never appear. See Data sources. | .

207.title: A reading is absent on this Mac
207.content: Available readings depend on the Mac model and macOS version: . | The SMC table has 61 candidate SMC keys. Every Mac is asked for 31 common SMC keys, Mac computers with Apple silicon for 4 more, and only the Mac17,9 with the t6050 chip for the 26 model-specific core and GPU temperatures. Keys that the SMC on this Mac does not have are left out. On the measured M5 Pro, 38 answer. | On any other model the plugin log records This model uses common typed sensors; its generation-specific catalog is not qualified. | A Mac without fans need not report fan readings. | If the SMC service is missing or cannot be opened, every SMC reading is absent while system counters work. The log says smc readings unavailable; other sources continue. and the support report’s sourceErrors names the step that failed. | Network rates are one sum over the interfaces named en followed by a number; there is no reading for a single interface or drive. | . For the state of Intel validation, see Hardware compatibility. To ask for a reading on your Mac, file an issue with the model and chip from the support report.

208.title: Values do not seem to update
208.content: Every read takes new measurements, and a reading older than 15 seconds is removed, never shown as current. A number that stays the same is usually a measurement that did not change. Check these: . | Read every is long. At 5 seconds a key changes at most every 5 seconds. Change it under Advanced, Connection. | The value is steady. Memory total and Startup volume total rarely change. How often the SMC itself refreshes a key is unknown, and a register that stopped changing internally cannot be told apart from a steady one. | The key is not visible. Nothing is read while no Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile is visible anywhere, and after 2 seconds like that reading stops. A page you return to after that starts with Reading sensors and new sparklines; a page back within the 2 seconds continues where it was. | The sparkline restarted. It starts again when Read every changes, after a status screen, when its reading was missing, and when you return to a page after no Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile was visible anywhere for 2 seconds. It holds up to 36 points spaced by reads. | The plugin is not answering. See The panel says the plugin is not responding. | .

209.title: A reading shows the wrong unit
209.content: Temperatures: each key and dial has its own °F checkbox under Display, Temperature. It changes only °C readings, and thresholds follow it. The sparkline is stored in °C and keeps its shape. Bytes and rates: Data units, under Advanced, Shared defaults, applies to every key and dial. Decimal (KB, MB, GB; rates in Mbps) shows rates in bits per second; Binary (KiB, MiB, GiB; rates in MiB/s) shows bytes per second. Memory, swap and startup volume readings follow the same choice. See Temperature unit and Data units.

210.title: Thresholds do not fire
210.content: Check these first: . | The threshold unit. Warn at and Critical at compare the current value in the reading’s own unit: °F when °F is on. Byte and rate readings compare the source number in bytes or bytes per second, before Data units rescales the display. 100 Mbps is 12500000; 8 GB is 8000000000. | The direction. By default the alert fires at or above the number. For readings where low is bad, such as a fan or available space, tick Alert when the value drops to or below these numbers (for fans and clocks). | A key with several readings. Only reading 1 is checked, and it recolors the whole key. | A dial. Warn, Critical and the bar ends apply only to readings in the unit that was on the dial when you last changed any of them, so a temperature limit never fires on a fan. Change a limit while the reading you want is on the dial. | What an alert changes. A dial stays in its theme: only the range bar’s fill, or an overview row’s value, turns amber or red. A key checks the live value even while it shows MIN, MAX or AVG, so a maximum past a limit does not color the key. See Alerts on a dial. | . A blank field turns that level off, and a decimal comma such as 70,5 is accepted. No alert shows while a status screen or Sensor missing shows. See Thresholds and alerts and Warn at and Critical at.

211.title: Detail view problems
211.content: A press set to open details shows the Stream Deck alert triangle. The plugin refused to open the view and left the key as it was: . | This deck type has no bundled detail profile. The key’s Press section says Sensor details are not available on this deck with the model, and the log says Detail entry refused: no bundled profile for device type and a number. | No sensor data is available and Details list is Every reading from this reading’s sensor or Readings matching a filter. Only A custom list opens without data. | The key has no reading selected, or, with Every reading from this reading’s sensor, its reading is missing. | Readings matching a filter has an empty Filter. | A detail view is already open or opening on that deck. | . Nothing happens on the first press. The Stream Deck app asks to install the deck’s detail profile the first time. Until you accept, the deck stays where it is; the plugin drops that attempt after 30 seconds without a message. Press again after accepting. The view says No detail / selected. The plugin restarted while the detail view was showing, so it no longer knows which reading opened it. Press the Back tile to return, then open the details again. A development link does not install the bundled detail profiles. See When a press does not open the page.

212.title: Dial gestures do nothing
212.content: . | The deck has no dials. Sensor Dial needs a Stream Deck + or Stream Deck + XL encoder. Regular keys use Sensor Reading. | No reading is picked yet. A new dial shows Mac Sensors / rotate to pick. Turn it or pick a reading under On the dial now in the settings panel. | Turns specifically do nothing. Check whether Ignore turns (protects against accidental bumps) is ticked, whether the dial shows pinned, whether its reading is missing (Sensor missing / waiting holds the saved pick), whether a status screen shows, and, with Gestures set to Custom, whether Turn is Do nothing. The list under Gestures says what each gesture does now. | . Synthetic gesture traces replay in software tests; checks of physical Stream Deck + dial gestures are pending. See Dial controls and presets and Hardware compatibility.

213.title: Mac Sensors is missing after install
213.content: . | Look in the right category. The actions list groups them under Mac Sensors: Sensor Reading and Sensor Control for keys, Sensor Dial for Stream Deck + dials. | Check the requirements in Installation and requirements. Update an older Stream Deck app. | Check that it installed. The installed plugin is the folder ~/Library/Application Support/com.elgato.StreamDeck/Plugins/com.lawrensen.mac.sdPlugin. | The same version was already installed. See the next section. | . Mac Sensors is not on the Elgato Marketplace yet. Install from the package as described in Installation and requirements.

214.title: Opening the same version again does nothing
214.content: When the package’s version equals the installed one, the Stream Deck app keeps the installed files and the running plugin, and its own log records (AlreadyInstalled) Plugin 'Mac Sensors'. That log is ~/Library/Logs/ElgatoStreamDeck/StreamDeck.log; earlier app sessions are in StreamDeck.1.log and up. Opening the package again therefore cannot repair an installation. To install the same version again, export a profile backup, remove Mac Sensors as described in Removing, then open the package. To update, open the package of a newer version.

215.title: High CPU, memory or a lingering process
215.content: The plugin runs one reader however many keys and dials are visible, and stops reading 2 seconds after none is (the log says Stopped (no visible actions)). | High CPU at 250 ms. At Read every 250 ms both sources are read four times a second and every changed face is drawn again. An earlier 1.0.1 candidate, measured as a development copy in the Stream Deck app on the M5 Pro with 32 single-reading keys, used 2.478% of one core at 250 ms against 0.668% at 1 second (PERF.md). Choose 1 second or longer under Advanced, Connection. | Memory. Over 24 hours with 32 single-reading keys at 1 second on the M5 Pro, the published 1.0.1.0, run as a development copy, peaked at 92.55 MiB of resident memory with 12 threads and 49 to 50 file descriptors (PERF.md). The earlier candidate peaked at 95.9 MiB in shorter sessions at 250 ms. If you see steady growth, note how many keys and dials are visible and the Read every value, and attach the log. | A plugin process stays after the Stream Deck app quits. The plugin checks for the app every 30 seconds. After two checks in a row find the app’s process gone, it asks the app directly and exits if no answer comes within 15 seconds. The Stream Deck app starts its plugins when it launches; a real app restart with Mac Sensors has not been observed yet. If a Mac Sensors process keeps running well after that, keep the log and file an issue. | .

216.title: Reading the plugin log
216.content: The Stream Deck app runs the plugin in its own folder, and the plugin writes its log there: . ~/Library/Application Support/com.elgato.StreamDeck/Plugins/com.lawrensen.mac.sdPlugin/logs/ . In Finder, choose Go, Go to Folder and paste the path. The newest file is com.lawrensen.mac.0.log. Each time the plugin starts, and when a file reaches 50 MiB, the files move up one number, up to com.lawrensen.mac.9.log. Each line is TIMESTAMP LEVEL Scope: message, for example: . 2026-10-16T04:38:05.415Z INFO MacSensors: Started (1000 ms interval) 2026-10-16T04:44:15.647Z INFO MacSensors: Stopped (no visible actions) . Useful lines: . | MacSensors: Started (… ms interval) and MacSensors: Stopped (no visible actions): the reader started for the first visible key or dial, and stopped 2 seconds after none was left. A page change inside those 2 seconds logs neither line. | MacSensors: Read interval set to … ms: each effective Read every change. | MacSensors: smc readings unavailable; other sources continue. (or public): a source answered with an error or with data that was already too old; its readings were removed and the other source kept serving. | MacSensors: smc read failed; retrying. or smc could not start; retrying. (or public): a read did not complete or could not be queued. | MacSensors: Node is running under translation; sensor interfaces follow the detected hardware.: macOS reports the Node process as translated. | MacSensors: This model uses common typed sensors; its generation-specific catalog is not qualified.: this model gets the common SMC table. | Device connected: "…" (…, 8x4) and Device known: …: one line per deck, with the name you gave it, its type and its key grid. | Detail entry refused: …: why a detail press showed the Stream Deck alert triangle. | Parent probe failed […], Parent watchdog disabled, watchdog standing down and Parent process gone, and the app did not answer: exiting.: the check that ends the plugin when the Stream Deck app is gone. Report the exit line if the app is still running. | Uncaught exception or Unhandled rejection: an unexpected error; please report it with the lines around it. | . The MacSensors warnings are logged once each time the reader starts. In the 24-hour observation on the M5 Pro the log had no WARN or ERROR lines (PERF.md). Developer switches use the MACSENSORS_ prefix and are read from the environment the Stream Deck app gives the plugin at start; normal use needs none. MACSENSORS_LOG_LEVEL accepts trace, debug, info (the default), warn and error; at debug the log also records where each key and dial appeared. trace needs a debug launch of the plugin; otherwise the plugin uses debug and the log says so. MACSENSORS_TRACE_EVENTS=1 writes redacted input traces to logs/trace-<process id>.jsonl. The log names your decks as the Stream Deck app names them and can carry raw device and action identifiers, for example in Detail entry refused: already active on …. Review it before you share it.

217.title: Copy a support report
217.content: In a Sensor Reading or Sensor Dial panel, open Advanced, then Support, and choose Copy support report. In a Sensor Control panel the button is under Advanced. The plugin builds the report on request and the panel copies it to the clipboard. The button then says Copied to clipboard, Copy failed, or Plugin not responding if no report arrived within 3 seconds, and returns to its label after 2 seconds. Nothing is uploaded. The report is JSON with these parts: . | Part | Contents | . | plugin, streamDeckApp, macOS | Installed plugin version, Stream Deck app version and macOS version | . | devices | Each deck by model, type, key grid, encoders and touch strip, with a hashed identifier | . | recentEvents | The last 24 recorded dial and Sensor Control events, with hashed device and reading identities | . | mac | Node version, process architecture, platform, kernel release, the Node path with your home folder shown as ~, Mac model, chip, Apple silicon, translation, and how many readings each source returned (sourceRows) with any source error (sourceErrors); catalog: "not sampled" before the first read | . | dataSource | Current state and reason, reading count, effective Read every, whether reading is running, how many actions keep it running, and the age of the oldest current reading | . | sensorDial, control, detailNav | Dial presets, views and set sizes, visible Sensor Control keys, and detail view state, by hashed identifiers | . How it reports the processor and translation: . | processArchitecture is arm64 or x64, the architecture the app’s Node runtime runs as. The plugin loads the matching native reader. | appleSilicon is true when macOS reports the arm64 flag (hw.optional.arm64) as 1, false when it reports 0, and null when macOS has no such flag, as on the hosted Intel runner. | translation is native when macOS says the process is not translated (sysctl.proc_translated is 0), or has no translation flag at all, as on an Intel Mac; translated when it reports 1; unknown for any other answer, with the error number in translationError. Before 1.0.1, Intel Mac computers reported unknown. | chip is the chip identifier from the device tree on Apple silicon, for example t6050, and unknown where the device tree has no such entry. | . The report leaves out sensor values, reading labels and names, deck names, raw device identifiers, your user name, serial numbers and hardware UUIDs. It also does not carry log lines, so attach the relevant log lines separately. Review the report before you post it.

218.title: What stays on this Mac
218.content: . | The plugin makes no internet requests and has no telemetry or update check of its own. Its only network connection is the Stream Deck SDK’s WebSocket to the Stream Deck app at 127.0.0.1, on the port the app assigns. | Settings are stored by the Stream Deck app. | The log and the support report stay on this Mac until you share them. The report reaches the clipboard only when you choose Copy support report. | . See also FAQ and privacy.

219.title: Before you file an issue
219.content: Check these first: . | The Mac meets the requirements in Installation and requirements; Hardware compatibility says what has been measured. | You chose Check again once, and quit and reopened the Stream Deck app if the screen stayed. | You picked the reading again if it is gone from this Mac for good. | Threshold values use the displayed temperature unit, or bytes and bytes per second for byte and rate readings, and Alert when the value drops to or below these numbers is ticked where low is bad. | . If it still fails, open a public issue on the documentation repository, name Mac Sensors in the title, and include: . | What you see: the exact status text, for example “Source busy / retrying”, or a photo of the key or dial. | The installed plugin version, from the support report’s plugin field, and where you got the package. | The Mac model, chip and macOS version, from the support report. | The Stream Deck app version and deck model, for example Stream Deck +. | Your Read every value, and how many keys and dials are visible. | The relevant log lines from com.lawrensen.mac.0.log, especially any MacSensors warnings. | The support report, pasted into the issue after you review it. | . Report security issues through the private security-report form, naming Mac Sensors and the affected version. Do not post vulnerability details in a public issue.

221.title: Troubleshooting
221.content: Start with the exact text on your key, dial or settings panel header. Mac Sensors reads this Mac directly; there is no separate sensor application to start or configure. | What you see | Go to | . | Reading sensors | Wait for the first read | . | Source busy | Check the first read | . | No sensor data | Check both sources | . | Tahoma needed | Install Tahoma Bold | . | Bridge failed | Reinstall the native reader | . | Source error | Collect the evidence | . | Needs macOS | Check the runtime | . | Sensor missing / pick again, or Sensor missing / waiting on a dial | Check the saved reading | . | Access denied, Not updating | Report it | . | Pick a sensor, or Mac Sensors / rotate to pick on a dial | Pick a reading | . | Saved reading not found (settings panel header) | Check the saved reading | . | The plugin is not responding | Restart the plugin | . For first-time setup, follow Getting started.

222.title: What changed in 1.0.1
222.content: 1.0.0.0 was the first release. 1.0.1.0 ships the same native readers, byte for byte. The changelog lists every change. | Change | What you see | . | Key statistics | A Sensor Reading key shows MIN, MAX and AVG instead of N/A, on a press or with Value shown on Minimum, Maximum or Average. Mac Sensors keeps them from its reads since the plugin last started reading sensors. Detail tiles show the same numbers. They start over after a gap in that reading. Sensor Dials keep their own session statistics as before. A key already set to a statistic shows numbers from its next read. | . | Page changes keep reading | Changing pages, opening sensor details or pressing Back keeps reading going: key MIN, MAX and AVG, sparklines, CPU usage and the rates carry on, and keys do not show Reading sensors. Reading stops 2 seconds after the last Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile leaves the deck. See When reading starts and stops. | . | One redraw per read | A key or dial that shows both system and SMC readings changes once per read instead of twice in quick succession, when both sources answer within 100 ms of each other. | . | Read every help | The setting under Advanced, Connection explains that one shared read updates every reading key and dial, that changing it clears sparkline history, and that shorter intervals use more processor time. | . | Read every limits | A blank value means the 1 second default. A stored value above 5 seconds runs as 5 seconds, so readings no longer expire between reads. | . | Counter readings sooner | CPU usage and transfer rates appear about a quarter second after reading starts, instead of one full read interval later. Reading starts when the first Sensor Reading key, Sensor Dial or detail tile appears, or when one returns after none was shown for 2 seconds. | . | No old values as live | When every reading lapses or fails before the first SMC read completes, keys and dials show Reading sensors instead of keeping old values as live. | . | Missing saved reading | A key whose saved reading this Mac does not report says Sensor missing and pick again. | . | Intel support reports | When macOS has no translation flag, as on an Intel Mac, the support report’s translation field now says native instead of unknown. Physical Intel validation is in progress. | . | Panel wording | Status text in the settings panel no longer names the plugin as the source of sensor data. The Text font line uses the same spacing as other fields. | . | Processor time | PERF.md compares an earlier 1.0.1 candidate, built before key statistics and the 2 second hold, with a rebuild of 1.0.0, each run as a development copy in the Stream Deck app 7.5.0 on the M5 Pro with 32 single-reading keys. The candidate used 0.668% of one core at 1 second against 0.855% for 1.0.0, and 2.478% against 3.164% at 250 ms. The published 1.0.1.0 used 0.704% at 1 second over a 24-hour observation. Performance and resource use has the limits. | . Nothing needs doing after the update, except on a key that shows Sensor missing / pick again: pick another reading under Reading. Unit tests, a mock Stream Deck host and a 24-hour observation on the measured Mac cover software behavior. They do not cover physical readability, dial gestures or Intel hardware behavior. Hardware compatibility lists what ran on which Mac and deck and what is still pending.
